Assessments of consumers’ past financial situation were likewise more negative (-16.0 vs. -15.1). Meanwhile, expectations for unemployment improved notably (33.2 vs. 36.2), while expectations for the general economic outlook became less pessimistic (-41.8 vs. -42.4). Assessments of the past economic situation also improved (-53.7 vs. -54.0). On the inflation front, perceptions of past price growth continued to ease (41.5 vs. 42.4).

title: Czechia Economy Grows 0.4% in Q2
summary: The Czech Republic’s gross domestic product expanded by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating from a 0.2% increase in the previous quarter but falling slightly short of market expectations of 0.5%, according to preliminary estimates. Growth was supported by higher final consumption expenditure and a positive contribution from the foreign trade balance, while gross capital formation weighed on the overall performance. Industry was the primary driver of quarter-on-quarter gross value added growth, with most service sectors also recording solid gains. On an annual basis, the economy grew 2.0% in the Q2 2026, easing from a 2.2% expansion in the previous quarter, driven mainly by stronger household final consumption expenditure and rising foreign demand. Industry made the largest contribution to gross value added growth, with additional support from the trade, transport, accommodation and food service, and information and communication sectors.

title: Sweden Consumer Morale Hits 18-Month High
summary: Sweden's household confidence indicator climbed to 97.1 in July 2026 from an upwardly revised 94.2 in the previous month. While the latest reading marked the highest level since January 2025, consumer sentiment remained somewhat subdued relative to normal levels, primarily weighed down by weaker expectations for personal finances over the next twelve months and a subdued willingness to make major purchases. Households also continued to regard buying a car within the coming year as highly unlikely. Meanwhile, the survey's remaining components were broadly in line with their long-term averages.

title: Austria Producer Inflation Rises Further in June
summary: Annual producer inflation in Austria rose to 3.1% in June 2026 from 2.8% in the previous month. This was the highest level since April 2023, mainly driven by rising prices for intermediate goods (6.6% vs 5.7% in May). Prices for consumer goods also increased 0.2%, following a 0.1% rise in the prior month. Meanwhile, energy prices rose for the third consecutive month, although at a slower pace than in May (2.1% vs 2.8%), while price growth for capital goods was unchanged at 1.0%. On a monthly basis, the PPI edged up 0.1%, easing from a 0.5% rise in May, as price increases for basic metals (2.0%) and paper and paper products (1.4%) were partly offset by declines in prices of chemicals and chemical products (-1.5%) and food products (-0.1%)

title: Austrian Economy Stalls in Q2
summary: Austria's economy stagnated quarter-on-quarter in Q2 2026, after expanding 0.2% in each of the previous two quarters, according to preliminary estimates. The stagnation reflected higher oil prices triggered by the Iran conflict, which interrupted the economic recovery. Household consumption weakened (-0.1% vs. +0.2% in Q1), while government spending also edged down (-0.1% vs. +1.6%). Gross fixed capital formation rose 0.4% after being broadly unchanged in the previous quarter. Net trade provided little support, with exports increasing 0.5% and imports rising 0.6%. On the production side, industrial output weakened (-0.1% vs. +1.3%) and construction contracted for a second straight quarter (-0.4% vs. -0.6%), while trade and tourism-related services recovered (+0.3% vs. -0.8%). Information, financial, insurance, and real estate services remained resilient (+0.8%). On an annual basis, GDP expanded 0.8%, easing from 0.9% in Q1.

title: Spain Inflation Rate Hits Two-Year High in July
summary: Spain’s consumer price inflation rose to 3.5% in July 2026, up from 3.2% in June and above the 3.4% market forecast, according to preliminary data. This is the highest rate since May 2024, fueled by rising costs for fuels, lubricants, and electricity, as renewed Middle East tensions push energy prices higher again. The core inflation rate, excluding unprocessed food and energy, also climbed to 3.0%, from 2.9% in June, matching May’s near two-year peak. Meanwhile, the EU-harmonized inflation rate reached 3.8%, surpassing the 3.7% expectation and remaining well above the European Central Bank’s 2.0% target.

title: US GDP Likely Expanded 2.1% in Q2
summary: The US economy likely expanded at an annualized rate of 2.1% in Q2, matching the pace recorded in Q1 and signalling continued resilience despite the conflict in the Middle East, elevated gasoline prices, and the impact of tariffs. Consumer spending is expected to have remained robust, accelerating from the previous quarter as larger tax refunds and the FIFA World Cup provided additional support. Business spending on equipment likely posted another quarter of double-digit growth, driven by continued investment in AI-related technologies. However, investment in structures is expected to have remained weak, contracting for a tenth consecutive quarter, while residential investment likely declined for a sixth straight quarter. Meanwhile, net trade is expected to have weighed on overall growth, possibly subtracting more than one percentage point from GDP.

title: Bank of England Poised to Hold Rates
summary: The Bank of England is widely expected to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% as policymakers weigh weak economic growth against the risk of renewed inflationary pressures stemming from the escalating conflict between the US and Iran. Although UK inflation eased to 2.6% in June, largely due to lower fuel prices during a brief lull in Middle East tensions, the recent resurgence in hostilities is expected to keep price pressures elevated and inflation above the Bank's 2% target. The outlook offers little support for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has pledged to reduce living costs but has yet to outline how those measures will be financed. Governor Andrew Bailey recently acknowledged concerns over the renewed conflict but said it had not materially altered the UK's inflation outlook. While most economists expect rates to remain unchanged through year-end, financial markets continue to price in a quarter-point increase by November.

title: Turkey Economic Sentiment Improves in July
summary: Turkey's Economic Confidence Index rose to 99.8 in July 2026 from 98.9 in the previous month, reaching its highest level since February and moving closer to the 100 threshold that separates optimism from pessimism. The improvement was driven by improving consumer confidence, which rose 2.2% to 89.8, alongside gains in the services sector (+1.4% to 112.0) and construction (+0.6% to 83.5). In contrast, confidence in the manufacturing sector slipped 0.8% to 101.2, while retail trade confidence fell 1.6% to 111.0. Despite the overall improvement, the headline index remained below the 100 mark, indicating that economic sentiment continued to point to a slightly pessimistic outlook.

title: DAX Falls on Earnings, Fed Split, and Middle East Tensions
summary: Frankfurt's DAX 40 declined 0.5% to 25,350 on Thursday as investors assessed a wave of corporate earnings, fresh economic data, escalating tensions in the Middle East, and growing uncertainty over the US interest rate outlook following a divided Federal Reserve decision. Adidas led losses, plunging 16% after the sportswear maker raised its revenue guidance but warned that higher costs would continue to weigh on earnings growth. Airbus also fell more than 2%, despite reporting strong second-quarter results, after the aircraft manufacturer merely reaffirmed its full-year targets. Meanwhile, renewed US airstrikes on Iran in response to attacks on American forces across the Middle East lifted oil prices and weighed on market sentiment. On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, though three FOMC members dissented in favor of a rate hike, adding to policy uncertainty.

title: Slovakia Business Morale Recovers in July
summary: The industrial confidence indicator in Slovakia rose by 8.7 points to 2.0 in July 2026, rebounding from a seven-month low of -6.7 in the previous month. The improvement was mainly driven by higher expected production (32 vs 17 in June), particularly in the manufacture of wood and paper products, electrical equipment, motor vehicles, trailers, semi-trailers, and other transport equipment. It was also supported by lower finished goods inventories (12 vs 25), mainly in the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products. Additionally, the employment outlook continued to improve (7 vs 2). Meanwhile, the current level of orders declined further (-14 vs -12), along with export order levels (-16 vs -15), while assessments of current industrial production eased (16 vs 28). Selling price expectations moderated slightly (10 vs 13).

title: Spain GDP Growth Rate Beats Forecasts in Q2
summary: The Spanish economy grew by 0.7% qoq in Q2, above 0.6% in Q1 and beating expectations of 0.6%, according to preliminary estimates, underscoring the economy's continued resilience and robust growth momentum. On the expenditure side, household consumption rose by 0.7% (vs 0.6% in Q1), government spending increased by 0.3% (vs 0.6%) and investment went up 0.5% (vs 0.1%). Exports increased 0.8% (vs -0.6%) and imports also rebounded, rising 0.6% (vs -0.9%). On the production side, all major sectors recorded growth. Industrial activity expanded by 1% (vs 0.4%), with manufacturing output rising 0.7% (vs 0.4%), construction activity increasing 0.6% (vs -0.2%) and the services sector growing by 0.8% (vs 0.8%). Meanwhile, the primary sector expanded by a modest 0.2%, following a 3.3% jump in Q1. Year-on-year, the GDP grew 2.7%, matching the pace of the previous three quarters and above forecasts of 2.5%. The Spanish government expects growth o remain above 2% through 2029.

title: Hong Kong Dollar Hits 4-week Low
summary: The Hong Kong Dollar touched 7.84 against the USD, the lowest since July 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, US Dollar Hong Kong Dollar lost 0%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 0.08%.

title: FTSE 100 Hovers at Record High Ahead BoE
summary: The FTSE 100 traded little changed on Thursday, holding near record levels, as investors awaited the Bank of England’s policy decision, with a flurry of corporate earnings driving sharp moves across the index. Shell rose around 1.5% after reporting its strongest quarterly profit since early 2022, while announcing a fresh share buyback. Rolls-Royce climbed more than 4% after raising its 2026 guidance, while BAE Systems gained about 2% after upgrading its sales outlook. Lloyds Banking added over 0.5% after beating profit forecasts, unveiling a 5-year strategy and announcing a £1 billion share buyback. Conversely, LSE Group fell more than 2.5% despite improving guidance and launching a £1.4 billion buyback. Haleon and BAT also declined, while Rentokil Initial slumped more than 15% after issuing an in-line profit outlook. Investors now await the BoE, which is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, following the Federal Reserve’s decision to keep policy steady.

title: Pound Slips Ahead of BoE Decision
summary: Sterling weakened to $1.334 on Thursday as investors awaited the Bank of England's policy decision later in the day. While the BoE is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, markets will closely watch the voting split and any guidance on the future policy path. Recent data showed UK inflation slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6% in June, below the BoE's forecast. However, higher energy prices have fueled concerns that inflationary pressures could re-emerge in the coming months. Meanwhile, fresh US airstrikes on Iran in response to attacks on American forces across the Middle East lifted oil prices and weighed on risk sentiment. The Federal Reserve also added to uncertainty on Wednesday by leaving interest rates unchanged despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: UK Gilt Yield Holds Above 5% Ahead of BoE Decision
summary: The UK 10-year gilt yield was little changed at 5.04% on Thursday, hovering near the two-month high reached last week as investors awaited the Bank of England's policy decision. While the BoE is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged, markets will focus on the voting split and any signals on the future policy outlook. Meanwhile, renewed US airstrikes on Iran in response to attacks on American forces across the Middle East lifted oil prices and dampened risk appetite. The Federal Reserve also added to market uncertainty on Wednesday by leaving interest rates unchanged, despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: Dutch Q2 GDP Growth Beats Forecasts
summary: The Dutch economy expanded by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 2026, accelerating slightly from the 0.3% growth recorded in Q1 and exceeding economists’ expectations of a 0.2% increase. The stronger-than-expected performance was driven mainly by domestic demand. Household spending rose by 0.5%, supported by higher purchases of passenger cars, food, beverages and tobacco, while business investment also increased by 0.5%, led by greater spending on electronic equipment despite weaker construction investment. Government consumption also contributed, rising 0.4% due to higher healthcare expenditure and public sector wages. External trade provided a small drag on growth, as exports increased by 1.2%, while imports rose even faster at 1.4%. On the production side, the strongest growth came from the trade, accommodation and food services, transportation and storage sectors, while manufacturing also performed well, particularly the machinery and petroleum industries.

title: European Stocks Rise on Thursday
summary: European stocks traded higher on Thursday, with the STOXX 50 adding 0.5% and the STOXX 600 gaining 0.4%, as corporate earnings remained the primary market driver. Investors also weighed additional US strikes on Iran, the resulting rise in oil prices, and the Fed's decision to leave interest rates unchanged for a fifth consecutive meeting on Wednesday. Markets also digested a fresh batch of economic data showing that France's economy rebounded in the Q2, while growth accelerated in Spain and the Netherlands. Meanwhile, Spain's inflation rate accelerated more than expected in July. Shell advanced 1.5% after reporting a sharp increase in profit, while L'Oréal gained 3% after posting better-than-expected quarterly sales. Schneider Electric surged 5.5% after raising its full-year targets, and BBVA climbed 2.2% after reporting an 11.4% increase in net profit. On the downside, Adidas slumped more than 16% after missing quarterly profit expectations.

title: Euro Falls on Data, Middle East Risks
summary: The euro weakened to $1.144 on Thursday as investors digested fresh economic data, escalating Middle East tensions, and uncertainty over the US interest rate outlook following a divided Federal Reserve decision. Spain's annual EU-harmonized inflation rate accelerated more than expected to 3.8% in July, the highest since May 2024 and well above the European Central Bank's 2% target. Meanwhile, France's economy grew 0.2% in the second quarter, rebounding from the previous quarter's contraction, while growth in Spain and the Netherlands accelerated to 0.7% and 0.4%, respectively, both exceeding forecasts. Meanwhile, renewed US airstrikes on Iran in response to attacks on American forces across the Middle East lifted oil prices and weighed on risk sentiment. The Federal Reserve also added to uncertainty on Wednesday by leaving interest rates unchanged, despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: Dutch Q1 Annual Growth Highest in 2 Years
summary: The Dutch economy expanded by 1.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, the lowest in two years, following a 1.4% increase in the previous quarter. Growth was primarily driven by public and household consumption. Government spending rose by 2.5%, while household consumption increased by 1.3%. Fixed investment also contributed positively, rising 0.4% from a year earlier. Meanwhile, exports grew by 2.5%, outpacing the 2.1% increase in imports, resulting in a positive contribution from net trade to overall economic growth. On the production side, the trade, accommodation and food services, transportation and storage, and public sectors made the largest contributions to GDP growth compared with the second quarter of 2025.

title: Energy Commodities Updates: Brent Crude Oil Rises by 1.48%
summary: Top commodity gainers are Brent Crude Oil (1.48%) and Crude Oil WTI (0.88%). Biggest losers are Natural Gas EU (-1.27%), Natural Gas UK (-1.25%) and Heating Oil (-1.09%).

title: Metals Commodities Updates: Iron Ore CNY Falls by 3.25%
summary: Top commodity losers are Iron Ore CNY (-3.25%), Titanium (-1.09%), Silver (-0.83%) and Gold (-0.51%). Gains are led by Copper (0.86%).

title: Bund Yield Nears 15-Year High on Oil Surge and ECB Rate Bets
summary: Germany's 10-year Bund yield rose to 3.18% on Thursday, approaching last week's 15-year high above 3.2%, as surging oil prices reinforced expectations that the European Central Bank could raise interest rates again this year. Energy prices climbed as the conflict between the US and Iran intensified, with a drone reportedly striking a US-owned gas storage tanker at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve added to market uncertainty on Wednesday by leaving interest rates unchanged despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike, while Chair Kevin Warsh offered no guidance on the future policy path. On the data front, stronger-than-expected GDP growth across major euro area economies and higher inflation readings in Germany and Spain reinforced expectations that the ECB could deliver a second rate hike this year, potentially as soon as September.

title: Agricultural Commodities Updates: Wheat Gains by 3.58%
summary: Top commodity gainers are Wheat (3.58%), Cotton (0.96%) and Canola (0.62%). Biggest losers are Rubber (-1.66%) and Rice (-1.10%).

title: Italy GDP Grows More than Expected in Q2
summary: The Italian GDP expanded by 0.2% in the second quarter of 2026, ahead of the median consensus of a 0.1% to mark the fourth consecutive period of growth. The result reflected some resilience to adverse macroeconomic developments in the period as the outbreak of war in the Middle East triggered a surge in fuel and natural gas prices, lifting borrowing costs faced by households, businesses, and the government. The expansion was supported by services, offsetting a contraction in both agriculture and industry. On the demand side, domestic consumption offset the negative impact from net foreign demand, with higher energy prices weighing on import turnover. On annualized terms, growth in the first half was 0.8%, firmly above the latest Bank of Italy forecasts of 0.5%.

title: Bulgaria Inflation Rate Eases in July
summary: The annual inflation rate in Bulgaria eased to 4.4% in July 2026 from 5.4% in the previous month, according to preliminary estimates. The slowdown was driven mainly by softer price growth for transport, slowing to 12.4% from 16.8%, and food, easing to 1.4% from 2.4%. Price growth also slowed for recreation and culture (7.4% vs 10.8%), restaurants and hotels (9.3% vs 9.6%), education (9.2% vs 9.4%), health (4% vs 4.3%), alcoholic beverages and tobacco (5.7% vs 6.7%), furnishings (0.3% vs 0.4%), and insurance and financial services (0.3% vs 2.7%). Meanwhile, inflation accelerated slightly for housing and utilities (5.1% vs 5%), while the decline in clothing and footwear prices softened (-0.4% vs -1%). On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.7% in July, rebounding from a 0.9% fall in June.

title: Swiss KOF Barometer Rises to Five-Month High
summary: Switzerland's KOF Economic Barometer rose to 103.5 in July 2026 from an upwardly revised 102.1 in June, beating market expectations of 101.0 and reaching its highest level since February. The reading points to improving momentum in the Swiss economy over the coming months. Strength was broad-based across the production side, with indicator bundles for financial and insurance services, other services, construction, and manufacturing all signaling a more favorable outlook. Indicators for foreign demand and private consumption remained broadly stable. Within the production sector, competitiveness, profitability, business conditions, and the assessment of production constraints all improved, but expectations for production activity and intermediate goods inventories softened. Within manufacturing, prospects weakened for the textile industry and the wood, glass, stone, and earth materials segment. The electrical industry and machinery and equipment continued to show stronger momentum.

title: German Economy Beats Expectations in Q2
summary: Germany's economy expanded by 0.2% in the second quarter of 2026, easing from an upwardly revised 0.4% growth in the previous quarter but surpassing market expectations of a 0.1% increase, according to preliminary estimates. Exports strengthened from the previous quarter, while household consumption remained subdued and capital investment declined. On an annual basis, the economy grew 0.9%, accelerating from an upwardly revised 0.7% expansion in the first quarter and also beating the 0.6% market forecast.

title: Wheat Rises By Over 3%
summary: Wheat prices climbed more than 3% to above $6.80 per bushel, approaching the two-year high of over $7 reached on July 22, as intensifying hostilities between Russia and Ukraine heightened concerns over grain exports from two of the world's largest wheat producers. The conflict has increasingly disrupted shipping activity in the Black Sea, prompting consultancy SovEcon to lower its Russian wheat export forecast for the current marketing season by around 4%. Russian authorities are also considering equipping grain vessels with machine guns and mobile missile systems to defend against Ukrainian drone strikes. Meanwhile, Ukraine continues to face Russian attacks on ships, ports, and other Black Sea infrastructure, with local farm groups warning of widespread bankruptcies if maritime exports remain suspended. These disruptions coincide with the regional harvest, threatening peak-season shipments and encouraging importers to source wheat elsewhere.

title: US PCE Prices Likely to Fall for the First Time Since 2020
summary: The US PCE price index is expected to decline 0.1% month-over-month in June 2026, marking its first monthly decrease since April 2020, after rising 0.4% in each of the previous two months. The ceasefire between the US and Iran in June helped ease energy-related inflationary pressures, leading to lower gasoline prices. The core PCE price index, which excludes food and energy, is projected to rise 0.2%, the smallest monthly increase in seven months, following a 0.3% gain in May. On an annual basis, headline PCE inflation is expected to ease to 3.7% from 4.1% in May, when it reached its highest level since April 2023. If confirmed, the June reading would be the lowest in three months. Core PCE inflation is also forecast to edge down to 3.3% from 3.4%, with May's reading having been the highest since October 2023. Despite the expected moderation in June, PCE inflation is projected to remain well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

title: Bulgaria Business Confidence Improves in July
summary: Bulgaria’s industrial business climate index rose to 17.2 in July 2026 from 16.1 in June, though it remained below the long-term average of 21.4. The increase reflected an improved assessment of the current business situation (20.4 vs 18.3 in June), while expectations for the next six months were unchanged at 14.0. Despite the better sentiment, current production activity (-5.4 vs -3.3) and total orders (-20.2 vs -17.9) weakened, with both domestic (-24.8 vs -22.1) and foreign orders (-26.5 vs -25.6) declining further. Production expectations eased (8.4 vs 8.7), employment expectations turned negative (-1.8 vs 0.7). Labour shortages (33.3% vs 32.4%) and weaker domestic (26.2% vs 25.3%) and foreign demand (25.3% vs 22.4%) became more pressing, while concerns over the uncertain economic environment eased (43.6% vs 46.9%).

title: Portugal Business Climate Steady in July
summary: Portugal's business confidence indicator stood at 2.8 in July 2026, unchanged from the previous month, when it reached its highest level since March. Confidence improved in construction and public works (4.6 vs 4.3), supported by stronger employment prospects and more favorable assessments of order books. Manufacturing sentiment also edged up, though remaining in negative territory (-4.3 vs -4.4). In contrast, trade confidence weakened to 3.7 from 4.2, reflecting less favorable assessments of sales volumes and activity expectations for the next three months. Meanwhile, confidence in the services sector eased slightly to 8.4 from 8.5, as weaker views on order books and demand prospects more than offset other factors.

title: Bulgaria Producer Inflation Eases Slightly in June
summary: Producer prices in Bulgaria rose 17.1% year-on-year in June 2026, easing slightly from an over three-year high of 17.5% in the previous month. Prices in electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply slowed to 20.4% from 21.5%. Meanwhile, mining and quarrying costs increased at a faster pace to 63.8% from 61.9%, as price growth in mining of metal ores remained elevated but slowed (105.3% vs 110.3%) and other mining and quarrying also moderated (4.9% vs 5.1%). Additionally, manufacturing inflation was unchanged at 8.9%, with notable increases in basic metals (25.6%), chemicals and chemical products (11.5%), and repair and installation of machinery and equipment (10.8%), while prices declined for machinery and equipment (-1.3%) and computer, electronic and optical products (-0.4%). On a monthly basis, producer prices fell 0.5%, following a 0.2% decline in May.

title: Portugal Consumer Confidence Edges Higher
summary: Portugal's consumer confidence index inched higher to -22.6 in July of 2026 from -25.9 in the previous month, extending the rebound from the over-two-year low of 27.1 in May. Despite remaining well below historical averages, the result was consistent with easing borrowing costs after the momentary resumption of energy exports from the Middle East. Improvements were noted in households' financial situation (-15 vs -16.2 in June) and the country's economic situation (-53.7 vs -55.1) over the last year. Future expectations also improved, with expectations on household financial situation (-8.8 vs -13) and macroeconomic conditions (-38.9 vs -45.6).

title: FX Updates: New Zealand Dollar Rises by 0.41%
summary: Top currency gainers are New Zealand Dollar (0.41%), South Korean Won (0.28%) and Dollar Index (0.08%). Biggest losers are Swiss Franc (-0.32%), Euro (-0.17%), Japanese Yen (-0.15%) and British Pound (-0.11%).

title: Zambia Inflation Rate Steady in July
summary: Zambia’s annual inflation rate stood at 6.5% in July 2026, unchanged from the previous month. It remained the lowest reading since February 2018 and stayed within the central bank’s 6%-8% target range, supported by a sharp appreciation in the kwacha, which has gained nearly 18% against the dollar this year on the back of surging copper prices and government efforts to encourage local currency usage. Inflation was also contained by the government’s decision earlier this month to extend a fuel tax moratorium through September 30, providing some relief as renewed tensions in the US-Iran conflict raised concerns over higher global energy and fertilizer costs. Food inflation eased to 6.4% in July from 6.7% in the previous month, while non-food inflation accelerated to 6.7% from 6.0%. On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.2%, slightly higher than the 0.1% increase recorded in June.

title: Greece Producer Inflation Slows in June
summary: Producer prices in Greece increased 8.8% year-on-year in June 2026, easing from a 13.5% rise in the previous month. The slowdown was driven mainly by a sharp deceleration in energy prices (15.5% vs 26.4%) and softer inflation for non-durable consumer goods (1.1% vs 1.6%). In contrast, price pressures strengthened for intermediate goods (6.4% vs 6.1%), capital goods (3.6% vs 3.4%), and durable consumer goods (2.2% vs 2.1%). On a monthly basis, producer prices fell 3% in June, following a 0.9% decline in May.

title: Cyprus Industrial Output Growth Eases Further in May
summary: Industrial production in Cyprus inched up 0.5% year-on-year in May 2026, slowing from an upwardly revised 1.9% increase in the previous month. The deceleration reflected weaker activity across mining and quarrying (0.5% vs. 4.5% in April), manufacturing (0.8% vs. 0.9%), mainly due to slower output of basic metals and fabricated metal products, electricity supply (0.0% vs. 8.3%), and water collection, treatment and supply (10.1% vs. 15.2%). Meanwhile, water supply reversed into contraction (-3.4% vs. 4.3%), while materials recovery remained in decline, with output falling at a steeper pace (-19.6% vs. -9.1%). For the January-May period, industrial output grew 1.5% compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.

title: Croatia Retail Growth Weakest Since 2023
summary: Retail sales in Croatia rose by 0.4% year-on-year in June 2026, easing slightly from a 0.5% increase in the previous month, remaining the weakest growth since March 2023. Sales of automotive fuels and lubricants fell at a faster pace (-12.9% vs. -11.8% in May). Moreover, retail sales via the internet or mail order declined sharply (-3.2% vs. 3.6%). On the other hand, sales increased for food, beverages, and tobacco (2.9% vs. 1.9%), while sales of non-food products excluding automotive fuels and lubricants rose after remaining flat in the previous month (at 1.5%). On a monthly basis, retail trade grew by 1.5% in June, rebounding from a 2.0% decline in the preceding month. For the first half of 2026, retail sales increased by 1.9% compared with the same period a year earlier.

title: Eurozone Economy Posts Strongest Growth in Over a Year
summary: The eurozone economy expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating from flat growth in the previous quarter and beating market expectations of a 0.2% increase, according to preliminary estimates. It marked the bloc's strongest quarterly expansion since the first quarter of 2025, as robust AI-related investment, solid government spending, and one-off factors helped offset the impact of the conflict in Iran and higher energy costs. Among the largest euro area economies, Spain once again led growth, with GDP rising 0.7%, up from 0.6% in the first quarter and above forecasts. The Netherlands expanded by 0.4%, twice the expected pace, while France returned to growth with a 0.2% increase after a 0.1% contraction. Germany and Italy also grew by 0.2%, easing slightly from the previous quarter but exceeding market expectations. Year-over-year, the eurozone economic growth accelerated to 1% in the second quarter from a revised 0.5% three months earlier, also above expectations.

title: Eurozone Unemployment Rate Holds at 6.3%
summary: The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in the Eurozone was at 6.3% for the fourth straight month in June of 2026, slightly under market expectations that it would be at a record low of 6.2%. The result maintained the period of stability in the currency bloc's labor market despite the surge in energy costs and interest rates in recent periods due to the outbreak of war in the Middle East. The number of unemployed individuals rose by 69 thousand from the previous month to 11.13 million. In turn, the unemployment rate for those aged under 25 years fell to 14.8% from 14.9% in the previous month. Among the largest economies in the Euro Area, the unemployment rate rose for Germany (3.9% vs 3.8% in May) and Italy (5.7% vs 5.3%), while it remained unchanged in France (8.2%) and fell in Spain (10.1% vs 10.2%) and the Netherlands (3.8% vs 3.9%).

title: Eurozone Industry Confidence Improves More than Expected
summary: The Euro Area industrial confidence indicator improved to -6.1 in July 2026 from -7.3 in June, outperforming market expectations of -7. Industrial sentiment across the Eurozone continued to strengthen, driven by more optimistic assessments from managers regarding future production and the current level of overall order books. However, views on finished goods inventories deteriorated slightly. Among the survey components not included in the headline confidence indicator, managers reported a sharp improvement in production over recent months. Sentiment toward export order books also became more positive, pointing to a gradual recovery in external demand.

title: Euro Area Consumer Confidence Confirmed at 5-Month High
summary: Consumer confidence in the Euro Area rose for a third straight month, improving to -15.9 in July 2026 from -17.6 in June, matching the preliminary estimate. Confidence across the broader Eurozone strengthened notably, supported by gains across all key components of the survey. Consumers expressed greater optimism about the economic outlook in their country, while assessments of both their past and expected household financial situation improved. Intentions to make major purchases also increased, reflecting a broad-based recovery in consumer sentiment.

title: Montenegro Trade Deficit Hits Record High
summary: Montenegro's trade deficit widened to €396.5 million in June 2026 from €366.4 million a year earlier. This marks the highest trade deficit on record, as imports rose 7.7%, outpacing a 3.2% increase in exports. In the first half of the year, imports increased 3.4% year-on-year to €2,177.9 million, driven mainly by higher purchases of mineral fuels, lubricants and related materials (12.3%), animal oils and fats (8.4%), chemicals (5.9%), and machinery and transport equipment (1.6%). Meanwhile, exports fell 7.4% to €261.4 million, weighed down by lower shipments of machinery and transport equipment (-39.1%), chemicals (-27.6%), and crude materials (-18.4%). Europe remained Montenegro's main trading partner, accounting for 94.3% of exports and 78.8% of imports.

title: Eurozone Economic Sentiment Improves More Than Expected
summary: The Economic Sentiment Indicator for the Eurozone rose to 96.9 in July of 2026 from the upwardly revised 95.4 in the previous month, ahead of the median market consensus of 96. It was the highest reading since February, reflecting an improvement in sentiment from the momentary drop in energy prices and borrowing costs on the short-lived truce in the Middle East war. The confidence indicator for services providers improved to 4.7 from the upwardly revised 4.2. Meanwhile, industrial pessimism softened to -6.1 from 7.5. Among the Euro Area's largest economies, the ESI rose for Germany (97.2 vs 91.6), France (95.9 vs 93.5), Italy (99.6 vs 99.2), and Spain (104.3 vs 103.5).

title: Chinese Yuan Hits 3-1/2-year High
summary: The Chinese Yuan touched 6.75 against the USD, the highest since February 2023. Over the past 4 weeks, US Dollar Chinese Yuan lost 0.59%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 6.32%.

title: Portugal's Economy Rebounds Strongly in Q2
summary: Portugal's economy expanded by 0.8% in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating from an upwardly revised 0.1% growth in the previous quarter, according to preliminary estimates. The rebound was driven by a positive contribution from net exports and stronger private consumption, although investment declined. The recovery followed a weak first quarter, when severe storms disrupted activity in central Portugal, while a surge in energy prices linked to the conflict in Iran weighed on growth. On an annual basis, GDP growth edged up to 2.5% from a revised 2.4% in the previous quarter. The government expects the economy to expand by 2.0% this year, while the Bank of Portugal projects slightly slower growth of 1.8%, following 1.9% growth in 2025.

title: South Africa Producer Inflation Eases in June
summary: Producer price inflation in South Africa rose by 7.5% in June 2026, easing from an over three-year high of 7.8% in the previous month. The slowdown was driven largely by decreases recorded in food, beverages, and tobacco (1.3% vs 2.1% in May), paper and printed products (8.5% vs 8.7%), electrical machinery, and communications and metering equipment (6.2% vs 6.9%), transport equipment (0.6% vs 0.7%), and furniture (4.6% vs 8.2%). On the other hand, costs increased for textiles, clothing, and footwear (6.9% vs 5.2%), non-metallic mineral products (11.5% vs 10.5%), and metals, machinery, equipment, and computing equipment (3.2% vs 2.9%), while inflation remained steady for coke, petroleum, chemical, rubber, and plastic products (at 22.0%). On a monthly basis, producer costs fell by 0.1%, following a 2.6% growth in the preceding period.

title: Belgium Annual Inflation Edges Up in July
summary: Belgium's annual inflation rate edged up to 3.56% in July 2026 from 3.4% in the previous month. Energy inflation accelerated slightly to 10.6% from 10.3%, while electricity prices rose at a faster pace (7.9% vs 6.2%). Additional upward pressure came from housing and utilities (4.6% vs 3.6%), driven in part by faster rent inflation (3.4% vs 3.2%), as well as recreation and culture (8.3% vs 8.1%), health (6.7% vs 6.6%), and insurance and financial services (2% vs 1.8%). Meanwhile, inflation eased for transport (5.5% vs 7.9%), restaurants and hotels (4.1% vs 5.9%), clothing and footwear (1.2% vs 2.3%), furnishings (0.1% vs 0.4%), and information and communication (1.6% vs 1.9%). Food prices fell 0.12% after rising 1.2% in June. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.63%, up from a 0.3% rise in the previous month.

title: Italy Jobless Rate at 7-Month High
summary: The unemployment rate in Italy rose to 5.7% in June 2026 from an upwardly revised 5.3% in May, exceeding market expectations of 5.1%. This marked the highest level since November 2025, as the number of unemployed individuals increased by 97 thousand from the previous month to a seven-month high of 1.46 million. Meanwhile, the employment rate remained unchanged at 62.9%, with the number of employed persons edging higher by 1 thousand to 24.31 million. Temporary employees increased by 91 thousand from the previous month, while permanent and self-employed workers declined by 46 thousand and 44 thousand, respectively. The youth unemployment rate, measuring jobseekers aged 15 to 24, picked up to 18.4% in June from a record low of 16.9% in May. The inactivity rate edged lower to 33.2% from 33.5%.

title: Montenegro Tourist Arrivals Climb 5.8% in June
summary: The number of tourist arrivals in Montenegro rose by 5.8% year-on-year to a ten-month high of 206,990 in June 2026, accelerating from 0.3% in the previous month. Foreign visitors remained the primary source of arrivals, accounting for 91.4% of the total, or 189,266 arrivals, while domestic arrivals represented 8.6%, or 17,724. Among foreign tourists, Europe continued to be the largest source region, contributing 78.8% of arrivals, led by Serbia, the United Kingdom, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Poland. Outside Europe, the largest numbers of arrivals were recorded from Israel, the United States, and China (including Hong Kong). By type of accommodation, seaside resorts remained the most popular area, accounting for 81.9% of arrivals, followed by the capital region (10.3%) and mountain resorts (4.7%). Meanwhile, overnight stays in collective accommodation totaled 793,956, with foreign visitors accounting for 90.8% of stays and domestic tourists accounting for the remaining 9.2%.

title: Italy Producer Inflation Slows in June
summary: Italy's producer prices increased 5.8% year-on-year in June 2026, easing from a 7.3% rise in the previous month. Domestic producer inflation slowed to 6.8% from 9.1%, while prices excluding energy accelerated slightly (2.9% vs 2.5%). Within manufacturing, price growth slowed for food, beverages and tobacco (-1.8%) and computer, electronic and optical products (-0.6%), while prices increased for coke and refined petroleum products (42.2%) and chemicals (8.0%). Meanwhile, inflation for electricity and gas supply eased to 8.9% from 12.6%. On foreign markets, producer prices accelerated to 3.1% from 2.7%, with prices rising 3.4% in the euro area and 2.8% outside it. Abroad, prices rose most for coke and refined petroleum products (18.1% non-euro area). On a monthly basis, producer prices were unchanged in June after a 0.2% decline in May.

title: Malta Producer Inflation Steady at 1.5% in June
summary: Producer prices in Malta increased 1.5% year-on-year in June 2026, matching the revised reading in the previous month and remaining at their highest level since October 2023 for a second consecutive month. Energy prices were unchanged from the previous month. Meanwhile, inflation eased for intermediate goods (2.7% vs. 2.9%) and capital goods (5.0% vs. 5.1%), while consumer goods prices were flat after declining 0.4% in the previous month. Within consumer goods, durable goods held steady at 0.1%, while non-durable goods were also unchanged after falling 0.5% in May. By market, producer inflation accelerated for both the domestic market (1.0% vs. 0.9%) and the non-domestic market (2.1% vs. 2.0%), although growth for exports to the Euro Area eased slightly (3.3% vs. 3.4%) while that for non-Euro Area markets picked up (1.0% vs. 0.8%). On a monthly basis, producer prices were unchanged in June, after rising 1.2% in the previous month.

title: Portugal Retail Sales Up 3% YoY
summary: Retail sales in Portugal increased 3% year-on-year in June 2026, following a downwardly revised 2.8% gain in May. Strong increases were recorded for household goods (7.5% vs 10.8%); textiles, clothing and footwear (8.1% vs 11%); computers, telecommunication equipment and books (4.2% vs 0.9%); pharmaceutical products and cosmetics (5.2% vs 5.7%) and for online and mail sales (17.1% vs 10.3%). Excluding fuel, retail sales increased 3.8%, compared to a 4.4% gain in May. Compared to the previous month, retail sales jumped 1.7%, rebounding from a 0.2% fall in May.

title: Oil Steadies After Thursday Rally
summary: Crude oil held above $84 a barrel on Thursday after surging 6.6% in the previous session, amid renewed US military action against Iran. President Donald Trump pledged retaliation following an Iranian strike on a US military base in Jordan, reinforcing concerns that the conflict could become more prolonged and further threaten energy supplies from the Persian Gulf. The escalation has also heightened risks to shipping through the Red Sea, a critical alternative trade route. US Central Command said its forces launched a major wave of strikes targeting dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps sites. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels continued to threaten Saudi Arabia, while Saudi forces joined US operations against Tehran-linked militants in Iraq. Adding to supply concerns, the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended oil loadings at its Black Sea terminal after two tankers associated with the facility were attacked overnight.

title: Oil Falls After Thursday Rally
summary: Crude oil fell below $84 a barrel on Thursday after surging 6.6% in the previous session, amid renewed US military action against Iran. President Donald Trump pledged retaliation following an Iranian strike on a US military base in Jordan, reinforcing concerns that the conflict could become more prolonged and further threaten energy supplies from the Persian Gulf. The escalation has also heightened risks to shipping through the Red Sea, a critical alternative trade route. US Central Command said its forces launched a major wave of strikes targeting dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps sites. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels continued to threaten Saudi Arabia, while Saudi forces joined US operations against Tehran-linked militants in Iraq. Adding to supply concerns, the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended oil loadings at its Black Sea terminal after two tankers associated with the facility were attacked overnight.

title: Ireland Harmonised Inflation at 5-Month Low
summary: The EU-standard Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices in Ireland rose 3.1% year-on-year in July 2026, easing from a 3.2% increase in the previous month and marking the lowest reading since February, according to preliminary estimates. The slowdown was driven by softer energy inflation, which decelerated to 6.5% from 10.0% in June. Meanwhile, the HICP excluding energy and unprocessed food accelerated to 2.9% from 2.5%, food price inflation edged up to 0.8% from 0.5%, and services inflation ticked higher to 3.7% from 3.6%. On a monthly basis, harmonised consumer prices were unchanged in July, following a 0.1% increase in the previous month.

title: Rio Tinto Stock Price Hits 4-week High
summary: Rio Tinto shares increased to 7179.00 GBp, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Rio Tinto gained 1.1%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 59.32%.

title: Euro Hits 6-week High
summary: EURUSD increased to 1.15, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Euro US Dollar gained 0.9%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 0.51%.

title: BoE Leaves Rates Unchanged, Flags Inflation Risks
summary: The Bank of England left its Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% at its July meeting, with a 6-3 majority in favor of holding rates steady, while three policymakers preferred a 25-basis-point increase to 4.0%. The decision reflects a balance between easing inflation and persistent risks from higher energy prices following recent tensions in the Middle East. Although consumer price inflation has slowed to 2.6%, the Bank expects it to rise again later this year as higher energy costs feed through to households and businesses. Encouragingly, there is little evidence so far of significant second-round inflation effects, while weaker labor market conditions and still-elevated borrowing costs are helping reduce underlying inflationary pressures. Nevertheless, the Committee believes inflation risks remain tilted to the upside due to geopolitical uncertainty and stands ready to tighten policy further if necessary to ensure inflation returns sustainably to its 2% target.

title: Pound Rises After BoE Holds Rates and Warns on Inflation Risks
summary: Sterling strengthened to $1.34, its highest level since July 20, after the Bank of England voted 6-3 to keep the Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75%, with markets having expected a narrower 7-2 split. The BoE said the impact of higher energy prices remains uncertain and warned that inflation is likely to rise later this year as energy costs feed through to the economy. It added that the risk of persistent inflation has increased, with the outlook now tilted to the upside, although developments in the Middle East could still materially alter the outlook. Meanwhile, fresh US airstrikes on Iran in response to attacks on American forces across the Middle East lifted oil prices and weighed on risk sentiment. The Federal Reserve also added to uncertainty on Wednesday by leaving interest rates unchanged despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: UK Gilt Yield Holds Near Two-Month High After BoE Decision
summary: The UK 10-year gilt yield held above 5.0%, remaining close to last week's two-month high after the Bank of England voted 6-3 to keep the Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75%, compared with market expectations of a 7-2 split. The BoE warned that higher energy prices are likely to push inflation higher later this year, with risks now tilted to the upside, although the outlook remains highly dependent on developments in the Middle East. Meanwhile, renewed US airstrikes on Iran lifted oil prices and weighed on risk sentiment, while the Federal Reserve added to market uncertainty by leaving interest rates unchanged despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: Spain Business Confidence Softens
summary: The seasonally adjusted industrial confidence indicator in Spain eased to -2.6 from the near two-year peak of -2.4 in the previous month. The pullback was centered around a 0.7 point decline in expectations of production over the next year, while price expectations rose by 1.2 points. Meanwhile, the index measuring order levels in the previous level rose by one point.

title: FTSE 100 Falls After BoE Decision
summary: The FTSE 100 closed slightly lower after reversing earlier gains, as investors digested the BoE’s decision to leave its Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% in a narrower-than-expected 6-3 vote. Corporate earnings drove most of the market action. Rentokil plunged more than 20% after saying full-year 2026 profit would be in line with expectations, with weakness in its UK asbestos removal business overshadowing solid growth in higher-margin pest control services. LSE dropped 7% despite announcing a £1.4 billion share buyback and slightly improving its sales outlook. BAT fell over 4%, while Haleon lost around 2.5% despite stronger-than-expected sales. Shell ended little changed after reporting its strongest quarterly profit since early 2022 and unveiling a new buyback. In contrast, Rolls-Royce surged more than 5.5% after raising guidance, BAE Systems gained about 2% on an improved outlook, and Lloyds Banking jumped 4% after beating profit forecasts and announcing a £1 billion share buyback.

title: FTSE 100 Hovers at Record High After BoE Decision
summary: The FTSE 100 traded higher on Thursday, hovering near a record high after the Bank of England voted 6-3 to keep its Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75%, compared with market expectations of a 7-2 split. Corporate earnings also drove market moves. Shell gained around 1.1% after reporting its strongest quarterly profit since early 2022 and announcing a fresh share buyback. Rolls-Royce surged more than 5% after upgrading its 2026 guidance, while BAE Systems advanced about 1% after raising its sales outlook. Lloyds Banking climbed 1% after beating profit forecasts, unveiling a new five-year strategy and launching a £1 billion share buyback. On the downside, LSE Group fell nearly 4% despite improving guidance and announcing a £1.4 billion buyback. British American Tobacco, Haleon, and Rentokil Initial also declined after earnings updates, with Rentokil plunging more than 16% on a cautious outlook despite meeting profit expectations.

title: US 10-Year Treasury Yield Continues to Rise
summary: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note edged up to 4.69% on Thursday, extending the previous session's 7bps increase and returning to its highest level since January 2025. Meanwhile, the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond surged to 5.23%, its highest level in 19 years, as investors continued to assess the latest FOMC decision and Chair Warsh's press conference. As expected, the Fed left the federal funds rate unchanged but three FOMC members voted in favor of a rate hike. While Chair Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to bringing inflation under control and stressed that policymakers would not hesitate to act if necessary, he was not among those advocating an immediate increase and refrained from offering clear forward guidance, leaving investors viewing the central bank as merely postponing what they see as an inevitable rate hike. The implied probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September has fallen to around 63%, down from nearly 80% before the Fed's decision.

title: Ukraine Raises Interest Rate by 50bps
summary: The National Bank of Ukraine raised its benchmark policy rate by 50bps to 15.5% in it July 2026 decision, its first rate hike in 16 months. The Board of the central bank stated that underlying inflationary pressures have risen in recent months and are likely to lift the headline inflation rate until the end of the year, warranting higher borrowing costs. The Board also noted that higher rates will increase the attractiveness of hryvnia-denominated assets and prevent higher levels of capital flight from households and businesses domestically. The NBU estimated that inflation could rise to the 10% level by the end of the year from the current 7.2% reading in June, before easing by next year. Meanwhile, expanded fiscal stimulus is expected to support economic growth, although inflationary responses are unlikely due to the impact of the Russian military attacks on aggregate demand.

title: Brazil Loan Growth Edges Up
summary: The value of outstanding loans from the Brazilian financial sector rose by 0.7% from the previous month to R$7.4 trillion in June 2026. Loans extended to corporations rose 1.5% to R$2.7 trillion, while household lending edged up 0.2% to R$4.6 trillion. On an annual basis, total credit expanded 9.7%, slightly above the 9.6% growth recorded in May. Household lending continued to outpace corporate credit, rising 10.8% year-on-year, although easing from 11.2%, while lending to legal entities accelerated to 7.9% from 6.9%. Meanwhile, credit with free resources totaled R$4.2 trillion, up 0.7% from the previous month and 7.5% from a year earlier, as stronger corporate lending partly offset a monthly decline in household credit, which nevertheless remained higher than a year earlier.

title: US Futures Rebound on Thursday
summary: Futures tracking US equities were firmly higher on Thursday, trimming losses from the previous session following a batch of corporate earnings. Contracts for the S&P 500 and the Dow were over 0.5% higher, while those for the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.5%. Microsoft surged nearly 10% premarket after posting a 43% growth in Azure revenue, the most since 2022 and ahead of expectations. This combined with capital expenditure forecasts that did not outpace expectations, limiting concerns of unsustainable AI spending. The result coincided with some respite for chip producers following their selloff yesterday, with Micron and Sandisk rising 3%. Conversely, Meta tanked 10% after its guidance missed expectations, while markets remained skeptical on whether its AI labs will drive revenue as signaled by the hyperscaler. Meanwhile, long-dated yields held their surge after the Fed Chair Warsh's reluctance to signal the Fed may raise rates triggered concerns that inflation could be higher for longer.

title: German Inflation Accelerates to Three-Month High
summary: Germany's annual inflation rate accelerated to 2.8% in July 2026 from 2.3% in June, exceeding market expectations of 2.7%, according to preliminary estimates. It was the highest reading since April, driven by a sharp pickup in energy inflation to 8.3% from 3.4% as renewed Middle East tensions pushed oil prices higher. Meanwhile, services inflation eased to 2.9% from 3.1%, while food inflation remained unchanged at 0.4%. Core inflation, which excludes energy and unprocessed food, edged down to 2.4% from 2.5%. The EU-harmonized inflation rate also rose to 2.8%, its highest level in three months and well above the European Central Bank's 2.0% target.

title: Euro Rises on Strong Eurozone Data and ECB Rate Hike Bets
summary: The euro strengthened to $1.148, its strongest level since June 17, as stronger-than-expected eurozone economic data reinforced expectations that the European Central Bank could deliver a second interest rate hike this year, potentially as soon as September, offsetting concerns over rising Middle East tensions and a divided Federal Reserve. The eurozone economy expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter, beating forecasts of 0.2% and marking its strongest growth since early 2025. Spain led with a 0.7% expansion, while Germany, France, and Italy each grew 0.2%. Firmer inflation readings in Germany and Spain also supported expectations of further ECB tightening. Meanwhile, renewed US airstrikes on Iran lifted oil prices and weighed on risk sentiment. The Federal Reserve added to policy uncertainty on Wednesday by keeping interest rates unchanged, despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: Bund Yield Holds Firm on Strong Eurozone Data and ECB Rate Bets
summary: Germany's 10-year Bund yield held above 3.15% on Thursday as stronger-than-expected eurozone growth and firmer inflation reinforced expectations that the European Central Bank could deliver a second interest rate hike this year, potentially as soon as September. The eurozone economy expanded 0.4% in the second quarter, beating forecasts of 0.2% and marking its strongest growth since early 2025. Spain led with 0.7% growth, while Germany, France, and Italy each expanded 0.2%, and the Netherlands grew 0.4%. Higher inflation readings in Germany and Spain further supported the case for additional ECB tightening. Meanwhile, renewed US airstrikes on Iran lifted oil prices and dampened risk appetite, while the Federal Reserve added to policy uncertainty by keeping interest rates unchanged despite three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

title: Mexican GDP Expands Most Since Q1 2022
summary: The Mexican GDP rose 1.5% from the previous quarter in the second quarter of 2026, rebounding from a 0.6% contraction in the first quarter of the year. This marks the strongest growth since the first quarter of 2022, exceeding market's expectations of a 1.2% increase. The increase was in line with Bank of Mexico's outlook, that left its interest rate unchanged amid easing inflation over the quarter. Growth was driven by primary activities, which rose 3.3%, while secondary activities expanded 4.6% and the services sector grew 1.5%. Economic activity increased 1.2% from the previous year, marking the strongest yearly expansion since the fourth quarter of 2023, supported mainly by primary activities.

title: Brazil Unemployment Matches Forecasts at 5.4%
summary: Brazil's unemployment rate fell to 5.4% in the rolling quarter ending in June 2026, down from 6.1% in the previous rolling quarter, matching market expectations and marking the lowest reading since January. The number of unemployed dropped 10.9% from the previous quarter to 5.9 million. Employment gains were concentrated in transportation, storage and postal services (3.9%) and public administration, education and health services (2.6%). The broader labor underutilization rate declined to 12.9% from 14.3%, while the number of underemployed workers fell 6.6% to 4.1 million. Total employment rose 1.1% to a record 103.1 million people, lifting the employment rate to 58.8% from 58.2%. Meanwhile, average real monthly earnings were unchanged from the previous quarter at BRL 3,738.

title: European Stocks Rebound
summary: European stocks extended their gains on Thursday amid strong GDP data and favorable corporate results. The Euro STOXX 50 added nearly 1% to 6,300 and the STOXX Europe 600 gained 0.7% to 649. The Eurozone GDP expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter, firmly above market expectations of 0.2% to reflect some resilience to soaring energy prices and sovereign yields in the period. Still, economic optimism was buffered by elevated EU-harmonized inflation rates, with pickups across Spain and Germany. Schneider Electric surged 9% after raising its full-year targets. BBVA climbed 3.5% after reporting an 11.4% increase in net profit. Also, ING rose more than 4% after posing their results, lifting other banks. Other banks also rallied. On top of that, Ferrari maintained its slight gains after raising its guidance. On the downside, Adidas slumped more than 16% after its heavy marketing campaigns around the FIFA World Cup triggered a surge in outlays.

title: US GDP Growth Slows in Q2
summary: The US economy expanded an annualized 1.5% in Q2 2026, below 2.1% in Q1 and forecasts of 2.1% the advance estimate from the BEA showed. Nonresidential fixed investment slowed (8.4% vs 10.6% in Q1). Investment in structures contracted for a tenth consecutive quarter (-5% vs -4.7%) and growth in intellectual property products also eased (8.8% vs 13.8%) while equipment investment remained robust (15.2% vs 15.8%). Meanwhile, residential investment rose 1.5%, marking its first increase in six quarters. Net trade exerted a larger drag (-1.01 pp vs -0.37 pp) due to a slowdown in export growth (4.5% vs 10.9%), while import growth remained strong (11.5% vs 11.8%). Government spending fell 0.8% (vs +4.4%) following sales of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Private inventories subtracted 0.67 pp from GDP growth. In contrast, consumer spending accelerated (3.2% vs 0.5%), led by prescription drugs, new light trucks, furniture, food services and accommodation.

title: US PCE Prices Fall as Expected
summary: The US PCE price index decreased 0.1% month-over-month in June 2026, as expected, after a 0.5% rise in May. Goods prices fell 0.6%, the most since November 2023, while services inflation slowed to 0.1% from 0.5% in the previous month. The core PCE index, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.1%, following a 0.3% advance in the previous month and less than market forecasts of a 0.2% rise. On an annual basis, headline PCE inflation eased to 3.7% from 4.1%, confirming expectations. Core PCE inflation edged down to 3.3% from 3.4%, also in line with forecasts.

title: US Initial Jobless Claims Below Expectations
summary: The number of people claiming unemployment benefits in the US were at 197,000 on the week ending July 25th, rebounding by 9,000 from the 57-year low in the previous period but still under median expectations of 200,000. Continuing claims, which are seen as a gauge of outstanding unemployment in the US, fell by 7,000 to 1,782,000 in the earlier week, below expectations of 1,800,000 to mark the lowest in over one month. The data continued to reflect a strong labor market in the US, aligned with statements from FOMC members that see the US economy in full employment. Meanwhile, initial claims filed by federal employees, which have been under scrutiny due the administration's efforts in decreasing the number of public workers, fell by 52 to 418.

title: Sanofi Stock Price Hits 4-week Low
summary: Sanofi shares decreased to 74.07 EUR, the lowest since July 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Sanofi gained 1.82%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 5.66%.

title: US Consumer Spending Growth Slows in June
summary: US personal spending increased by $65.2 billion, or 0.3%, in June 2026 from the previous month, slowing from an upwardly revised 0.9% gain in May, largely due to a sharp decline in gasoline spending as lower crude oil prices followed peace negotiations between the US and Iran. Goods spending rose $7.0 billion, as a $48.1 billion drop in spending on gasoline and other energy goods was partly offset by higher outlays on motor vehicles and parts (up $17.4 billion) and recreational goods and vehicles (up $13.8 billion). Meanwhile, services spending increased $58.2 billion, driven by health care (up $22.8 billion), financial services and insurance (up $14.0 billion), transportation services (up $7.1 billion), and recreation services (up $6.7 billion). Meanwhile, inflation-adjusted consumer spending advanced 0.4% in June, the same pace as in the previous period.

title: US Personal Income Rises Less Than Expected
summary: US personal income rose 0.2% month-over-month in June 2026, falling short of market expectations for a 0.3% increase and slowing from a 0.7% gain in May. The increase was driven by higher employee compensation, income receipts on assets, and government social benefits, partly offset by a decline in farm proprietors' income. Employee compensation rose by $32.3 billion, led by a $19.6 billion increase in private-sector wages and salaries. Income from assets increased on higher dividend and interest earnings, while government social benefits were supported mainly by higher Medicare and social security benefits. The decline in farm proprietors' income reflected the timing of payments under the American Relief Act of 2025. Meanwhile, disposable personal income also rose 0.2%, slowing from 0.7% in May, while real disposable personal income increased 0.3%, accelerating from a 0.2% gain in the previous month.

title: US Futures Hold Rebound
summary: Futures tracking US equities held their rebounds on Thursday from sharp losses yesterday amid a batch of corporate earnings and respite for chip stocks. The S&P 500 and the Dow were over 0.5% higher, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.5%. Microsoft surged nearly 10% premarket after posting a 43% growth in cloud revenues, the most since 2022. This combined with capital expenditure forecasts that did not outpace expectations, limiting concerns of unsustainable AI spending. Also, chip producers enjoyed some respite following their selloff yesterday with Micron and Sandisk rising 3%. Conversely, Meta tanked 10% after its guidance missed expectations, while markets remained skeptical on whether its AI labs will drive revenue as signaled by the hyperscaler. Meanwhile, long-dated yields held their surge despite softer-than-expected GDP growth in Q1. The Fed held rates yesterday, but Chair Warsh's reluctance to signal a rate hike raised concerns that inflation could be higher for longer.

title: TSX Futures Gain as Corporate Earnings Roll In
summary: Futures tracking the S&P/TSX Composite Index moved higher on Thursday as investors assessed a fresh round of corporate earnings. Vermilion Energy, Kinross Gold, Cenovus, Alamos Gold, Loblaw, and TransCanada reported results above expectations. In contrast, Ivanhoe Mines and Tourmaline Oil missed earnings estimates. Canadian Natural Resources and Fairfax Financial are due to report later in the session. Gold prices rose, supporting mining stocks. Meanwhile, minutes from the Bank of Canada's July 15th policy meeting showed policymakers were divided over the sustainability of the economic recovery. Separately, Prime Minister Mark Carney downplayed the possibility of restricting oil exports to the US as leverage in trade negotiations.

title: Canada Weekly Earnings Growth Slows in May
summary: Average weekly earnings of Canadian non-farm payroll employees rose 3.4% year-on-year to C$1,337.77 in May 2026, easing from a 3.8% increase in April and marking the slowest growth since February. The strongest wage gains were recorded in management of companies and enterprises (10%), utilities (9.2%), information and cultural industries (8.3%), retail trade (8.1%), and transportation and warehousing (7.1%). In contrast, earnings declined in real estate and rental and leasing (-1.8%) and construction (-0.1%). By province, Nunavut posted the largest increase (6.6%), followed by Nova Scotia (5.3%), Manitoba (4.8%), British Columbia (4.6%), and Prince Edward Island (4.5%), while Newfoundland and Labrador recorded a 1.3% decline. On a monthly basis, average weekly earnings fell 0.4%. Meanwhile, average weekly hours worked were unchanged at 33.4 hours.

title: US Real Consumer Spending Holds Steady at 0.4% in June
summary: Inflation-adjusted US personal spending rose 0.4% month-over-month in June 2026, matching May's pace. Goods spending accelerated to 0.7% from 0.6%, driven by stronger gains in motor vehicles and parts (2.2% vs. 1.9%), gasoline and other energy goods (0.7% vs. -3.3%), and clothing and footwear (1.3% vs. 0.9%). Meanwhile, services spending increased 0.3%, unchanged from May. Faster growth in recreation services (0.9% vs. 0.2%) and financial services and insurance (0.6% vs. 0.4%) offset slower gains in food services and accommodations (0.3% vs. 0.9%) and housing and utilities (0.0% vs. 0.2%). Spending on health care and transportation services remained steady at 0.3% each.

title: US 30-Year Bond Yield Surges to 19-Year High
summary: The yield on the 30-year US Treasury bond surged to above 5.2%, the highest since 2007, to reflect concerns of higher inflation in the longer term. The Federal Reserve held rates unchanged in its July meeting, aligned with the consensus, despite rate futures showing that one third of the market was positioned for a hike. The rise for the 30-year tenure led the movements among Treasuries following controversial statements by Fed Chairman Warsh during the press conference. The reluctance to signal a rate hike as the Fed's preferred response to inflation drove long-dated yields to surge, even though those on shorter maturities fell. The Chair also signaled a positive response in seeing long-term yields rise in Q2, akin to a policy tool, despite signaling the contrary in his speech during the ECB central bank forum one month prior. Underlying inflation gauges in the US flared higher in Q2 after tariffs and soaring energy prices lifted costs among various industries in the second quarter.

title: Gold Extends Gains on Softer Dollar
summary: Gold climbed to $4,080 per ounce on Thursday, extending Wednesday's 2% rally as a weaker US dollar provided support, while investors assessed the Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged and monitored escalating tensions in the Middle East. The Fed kept rates at 3.50%-3.75%, with Chair Kevin Warsh reaffirming the central bank's commitment to bringing inflation down. Meanwhile, the US military said it struck dozens of IRGC targets in Iran after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at US troops in Jordan, raising concerns over renewed inflationary pressures. Although gold is widely viewed as a hedge against inflation and geopolitical uncertainty, expectations of higher interest rates for longer tend to weigh on the non-yielding metal. Markets are currently pricing in roughly a 60% chance of a Fed rate hike in September. Separately, the World Gold Council said unofficial gold inflows into India have risen since the country increased import tariffs earlier this year.

title: HSBC Holdings Stock Price Hits 27-year High
summary: HSBC Holdings shares increased to 1590.00 GBp, the highest since July 1999. Over the past 4 weeks, HSBC Holdings gained 10.34%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 72.24%.

title: Dollar at 6-Week Low
summary: The dollar index extended its losses to around 100.3 on Thursday, its lowest level in about six weeks, after falling 0.6% in the previous session. Investors continued to assess the latest FOMC decision and Fed Chair Warsh's press conference. As expected, the Fed left the federal funds rate unchanged, although three FOMC members voted in favor of a rate hike. While Chair Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to bringing inflation under control and stressed that policymakers would not hesitate to act if necessary, he was not among those advocating an immediate increase and refrained from providing clear forward guidance. As a result, investors further scaled back expectations for an imminent rate hike and increasingly viewed the central bank as merely postponing what they see as an inevitable increase in borrowing costs. The implied probability of a 25-basis-point hike in September has fallen to around 55%, down from nearly 80% before the Fed's decision.

title: Baltic Dry Rebounds on Thursday
summary: The Baltic dry index rose 1.6% to 2,673 on Thursday, recovering from three consecutive sessions of losses. The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, advanced 2.5% to 4,167. Also, the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, increased 2.3% to 2,040, its highest level since July 24. On the other hand, the supramax index decreased 1.1% to 1,610, its lowest level in three weeks.

title: TSX Edges Higher on Financials and Miners Gains
summary: The S&P/TSX Composite Index edged higher to trade above 35,000 on Thursday, supported by gains in financial and mining stocks. Financials advanced, with RBC, TD Bank, CIBC, and Scotiabank up about 1% each. Gold prices rose, lifting miners, with Barrick and Franco-Nevada gaining nearly 1%. Technology stocks were mostly lower, with Shopify down 3% and Constellation Software losing nearly 4%, tracking weakness in US software application shares after Meta's guidance disappointed investors. In contrast, Celestica surged 6%, following a rally in US chipmakers. On the earnings front, Vermilion Energy (+2.5%), Kinross Gold (+0.2%), Cenovus (+0.3%), Alamos Gold (-2%), and Loblaw (-0.5%) reported results above expectations, while Ivanhoe Mines (+0.1%) and Tourmaline Oil (-3%) missed estimates. Canadian Natural (-0.5%) and Fairfax Financial (-1%) are due to report after the market close.

title: TotalEnergies SE Stock Price Hits 7-week High
summary: TotalEnergies SE shares increased to 78.50 EUR, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, TotalEnergies SE gained 14.11%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 44.6%.

title: US Natural Gas Stocks Rise Less Than Expected
summary: US energy firms injected 28 billion cubic feet (bcf) of natural gas into storage in the week ended July 24, 2026, below market expectations for a 35 bcf build, according to EIA data. Total working gas in storage rose to 3.084 trillion cubic feet. Inventories were 1% below levels recorded a year earlier but remained 6.4% above the five year seasonal average, pointing to relatively comfortable supply conditions. The latest build followed a 32 bcf injection in the previous week ended July 17.

title: US Natgas Prices Edge Up Slightly After EIA Data
summary: US natural gas prices edged higher to around $2.75 per MMBtu after the latest EIA report showed a smaller-than-expected increase in storage last week. Energy firms added 28 billion cubic feet of gas in the week ended July 24, below market expectations for a 35 bcf build. Despite the modest rebound, prices remained near their lowest level since early May as inventories stayed 6.4% above the five-year seasonal average, indicating ample supply. Production also remained strong, with output in the Lower 48 states averaging 110.6 bcfd so far in July, matching the record monthly high set in December 2025. LNG export demand softened slightly, with flows to major export terminals averaging 17.2 bcfd, down from 17.4 bcfd in June, partly because of scheduled maintenance at Freeport LNG’s Texas facility. Updated weather forecasts calling for cooler temperatures across the central and eastern US in the coming weeks also weighed on prices by reducing expected air-conditioning demand.

title: Qualcomm Stock Price Hits 13-week Low
summary: Qualcomm shares decreased to 146.30 USD, the lowest since April 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Qualcomm lost 18.15%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 4.91%.

summary: Top currency gainers are Japanese Yen (2.52%), New Zealand Dollar (1.13%), Brazilian Real (1.10%), British Pound (0.40%) and Euro (0.31%). Biggest loser is Dollar Index (-0.74%).

title: Colombia Industrial Confidence Improves
summary: Colombia’s industrial confidence indicator rose by 2.8 percentage points to -0.1% in June 2026, marking its strongest reading since February. The improvement was driven by a 12.9 percentage point increase in production expectations for the next quarter and a 1.7 percentage point decline in inventory levels, partly offset by a 6.2 percentage point drop in current order volumes. Compared with June 2025, the industrial confidence indicator declined by 1.6 percentage points.

title: Oil Eases After Thursday Rally
summary: Crude oil traded around $84 per barrel on Thursday after surging 6.6% in the previous session, as markets balanced renewed geopolitical tensions against signs that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz were improving. According to Kpler, 14 commodity vessels transited Hormuz in both directions on Wednesday, up from single-digit levels seen last week. Meanwhile, ample crude inventories in China continued to limit import demand, easing some supply concerns. Still, US forces struck dozens of Iranian military targets in an effort to curb Tehran’s ability to threaten regional shipping and US allies. Also, the East-West pipeline to bypass Hormuz that Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on now faces risks from Iran-backed Houthis. On top of that, the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended oil loadings at its Black Sea terminal after two tankers associated with the facility were attacked overnight.

title: Canadian Dollar Hits 6-week High
summary: The Canadian Dollar touched 1.40 against the USD, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, US Dollar Canadian Dollar lost 1.49%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 1.05%.

title: DAX 40 Rises to Over 3-Week High
summary: The DAX 40 advanced more than 0.5% to trade above 25,600 on Thursday, reaching its highest level since the record highs of early July, as investors welcomed upbeat economic data and a rebound in semiconductor stocks. Germany’s economy expanded by 0.2% in Q1, exceeding expectations for 0.1% growth, while annual inflation accelerated to 2.8% in July from 2.3%, also topping forecasts. Infineon surged nearly 10%, leading gains as chipmakers recovered from recent losses. However, Adidas slumped 13% after lifting its revenue outlook but warning that rising costs would weigh on earnings growth. Airbus also declined around 3%, despite reporting solid second-quarter results, as investors were disappointed the aircraft manufacturer only reaffirmed, rather than upgraded, its full-year guidance.

title: US 30-Year Mortgage Rate Extends Weekly Climb
summary: The average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage in the US rose to 6.66% as of July 30, 2026, from 6.58% a week earlier, marking the fourth consecutive weekly increase. According to Freddie Mac Chief Economist Sam Khater, the housing market continues to benefit from rising inventory levels, giving prospective homebuyers more options and supporting demand despite fluctuating mortgage rates. A year earlier, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate stood at 6.72%. Meanwhile, the average rate on a 15-year fixed mortgage increased to 6.04% from 5.96% the previous week.

title: Japanese Yen Rebounds on Likely Intervention
summary: The Japanese yen surged past 160 per dollar on Thursday from the 40-year low of 164 in the prior session amid the likely intervention by the Ministry of Finance. The probable move followed the $74.2 billion in selling by the MoF on the month to May 27th. This brought relief to recent pressure from high energy prices, fiscal concerns, and wide interest rate differentials. Soaring LNG and petrol prices due to the war in Iran raised dollar bids in Japan by energy importers and pressured growth due to lower margins, pressuring the domestic currency. In the meantime, fiscal concerns were magnified by the domestic tax panel reiterating the proposal to cut food taxes to 1% from the current 8%, adding to the supply of yen through fresh debt. Lastly, the Bank of Japan is due to hold rates unchanged tomorrow following their hike in June. The BoJ is expected to still deliver hikes this year, but the expectation of hikes by the US Fed limited any narrowing in the rate differential.

title: Oil Prices Down on Thursday
