EU storage facilities are about 55% full, below the seasonal five-year average and behind the pace needed to comfortably meet pre-winter storage targets before the heating season begins in November.

title: Swiss Retail Sales Growth Slows in June
summary: Retail sales in Switzerland rose by 1.5% year-on-year in June 2026, falling short of market expectations for a 3.2% increase and slowing from a downwardly revised eleven-month high of 3.4% gain in the previous month. The slowdown reflected weaker momentum across most retail categories, with overall retail trade excluding service stations easing to 1.5% from 3.2% in May. Among non-food retailers, turnover growth also slowed to 1% from 3.8%, largely driven by declines in sales of other goods (-1.9% vs 5.3%) and via mail order and the internet (-3.7% vs 6.0%). At the same time, revenues for food, beverages and tobacco moderated to 2.1% from 2.5%, while activity at service stations remained weak, declining 9.6% after a 6.1% drop in May. On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, retail sales grew by 0.2% in June, slowing from an upwardly revised 0.9% gain in the preceding period.

title: France Inflation Rate Unexpectedly Picks Up
summary: The annual inflation rate in France accelerated to 2.1% in July 2026, defying market expectations that it would hold at June's 1.8%, according to preliminary estimates. The pickup was mainly driven by faster increases in services prices (2.3% vs. 1.9% in June), particularly for accommodation and communication services, alongside stronger energy inflation (12.4% vs. 11.0%) amid higher gas and petroleum product prices. Meanwhile, the decline in manufactured goods prices eased (-0.7% vs. -1.1%), partly reflecting less pronounced seasonal sales effects, while food inflation held steady at 0.9% and tobacco inflation remained unchanged at 3.3%. On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.6%, rebounding from a 0.3% decline in June, driven by seasonal increases in transport and accommodation services as well as higher energy prices. The EU-harmonised annual inflation rate also accelerated to 2.4% from 2.0%, while the monthly HICP increased 0.6% after falling 0.3% in June.

title: French Producer Prices Drop 0.6% in June
summary: French domestic producer prices decreased 0.6% month-on-month in June 2026, following a revised 0.2% fall in May. Prices of manufactured products dropped by 0.6%, reversing a 0.1% increase in the previous month, largely due to a sharper decline in coke and refined petroleum products (-12.0% vs. -7.3%). Price growth also eased in the manufacture of food products, beverages, and tobacco (0.1% vs. 0.2%), electrical and electronic equipment, computers, and machinery (0.2% vs. 0.3%), and other manufactured products (0.2% vs. 0.9%), while prices for transport equipment were unchanged. Prices for mining and quarrying, energy, and water continued to decline, although at a slower pace (-0.7% vs. -1.0%). On an annual basis, domestic producer prices increased 2.6% in June, easing from a revised 3.1% rise in the prior month.

title: India Yield Retreats on Softer Oil
summary: The yield on India’s 10-year G-Sec edged down to around 6.8%, retreating from recent gains as softer crude oil prices and lower US Treasury yields improved demand for sovereign debt. Brent crude fell about 1.5% to around $87.7 per barrel, extending the previous session’s 1.8% decline, as continued tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea eased supply concerns despite stalled US-Iran talks. Meanwhile, the US 10-year Treasury yield slipped to around 4.65%, reversing part of Thursday’s surge after signs of progress toward a potential peace plan in Gaza reduced safe-haven demand, and falling oil prices reinforced the decline in yields. However, gains in Indian bonds remained limited as investors awaited New Delhi’s INR 340 billion auction of the benchmark 10-year bond and next week’s Reserve Bank of India policy decision, where the central bank is widely expected to keep its key policy rate unchanged.

title: Georgia GDP Growth at 3-Month High
summary: Georgia’s economy expanded by 8.6% year-on-year in June 2026, marking the fastest pace since March and accelerating from a 6.4% growth in the previous month. Economic activity remained supported by strong performances across several key sectors, with manufacturing, transportation and storage, construction, information and communication, and financial and insurance activities contributing the most to growth. In contrast, mining and quarrying, as well as the energy sector, contracted from a year earlier. In the second quarter of 2026, the economy expanded by an average of 7.5%, bringing average real GDP growth for the first six months of 2026 to 7.9%. External trade remained supportive in the January-June 2026 period, with exports rising 20.0% year-on-year to $3.88 billion, while imports increased 0.7% to $9.05 billion, lifting total merchandise trade turnover by 5.8% to $12.93 billion.

title: Turkish Tourism Revenues Drop 2.6% in Q2
summary: Tourism revenues in Turkey fell 2.6% year-on-year to USD 15.9 billion in the second quarter of 2026. Individual expenditures accounted for USD 10.9 billion of total tourism revenue, while package tour expenditures amounted to USD 4.7 billion. The largest share of spending was on package tours (30.2%), followed by food and beverages (21%), international transportation (12.4%), and accommodation (11.3%). Compared with the same quarter last year, spending on accommodation increased by 11.7%, while food and beverage spending rose by 5.2%. Meanwhile, spending on package tours declined by 5.5%, and transportation spending fell by 6.1%.

title: Nickel Holds Near 1-Month High
summary: Nickel traded around $17,300 per tonne in late July, remaining near its highest level in over a month and up more than 5% over the month as supply concerns in Indonesia supported prices. Indonesian smelters operated by Tsingshan Holding Group, the world's largest nickel producer, suspended some export loadings of mixed hydroxide precipitate and disrupted exports of other nickel products as authorities increased inspections over possible rare-earth content in shipments. The delays raised concerns over potential supply disruptions in the world's largest nickel-producing country, although the government moved to resolve regulatory bottlenecks by coordinating with industry participants and government agencies. Additionally, expectations of tighter Indonesian production controls and higher sulfur costs continued to support prices.

title: Stocks in France Hit 22-week High
summary: FR40 increased to 8561.00 Index Points, the highest since February 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, France Stock Market Index (FR40) gained 2.65%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 13.41%.

title: DAX Ends July Near Record High
summary: Frankfurt's DAX 40 climbed 0.8% to 25,800 on the final trading session of July, reaching its highest level since the record peak set earlier this month and putting the index on track for a monthly gain of more than 3%. The advance was driven by a strong rebound in technology stocks, broadly upbeat corporate earnings, and a continued sharp decline in oil prices, despite persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Chipmaker Infineon led the benchmark with a gain of more than 6%, followed by Siemens Energy and Hochtief, both of which advanced 3.7%. On the downside, Siemens Healthineers fell more than 2% after lowering its fiscal 2025/26 revenue guidance due to continued weakness in its diagnostics business. Elsewhere, defense electronics company Hensoldt reported that order intake more than doubled year over year, sportswear manufacturer Puma reaffirmed its full-year guidance despite weaker demand, and wafer producer Siltronic posted strong quarterly results.

title: Turkey Trade Deficit Widens in June
summary: Turkey’s trade deficit widened to $10.4 billion in June 2026 from $8.2 billion in the corresponding month a year ago, confirming preliminary data. The shortfall was the largest since March, as import growth outpaced the increase in exports. Imports jumped 23% year-on-year to a six-month high of $35.3 billion, amid a sharp rise in imports of intermediate goods (30%) and capital goods (19.6%), which more than offset a decline in consumer goods imports (-1.2%). The top sources of imports were China (15%), Russia (10.4%), Germany (7.0%), the US (5.3%), and Italy (3.9%). Exports grew 21.7% to $24.9 billion, driven mainly by a 20.2% increase in manufacturing exports. Exports of agriculture, forestry and fishing (48.4%) and mining and quarrying (41.4%) also went up. The main export partners were Germany (7.9%), the US (6.2%), Italy (5.4%), the UK (5%), and Spain (4.5%). In the first half of 2026, the trade deficit widened to $53.1 billion from $49.5 billion last year.

title: Rupiah Set to Post Fifth Consecutive Monthly Loss
summary: The Indonesian rupiah hovered near IDR 18,050 per U.S. dollar on Friday afternoon, holding steady from the prior session as traders looked ahead to busy domestic data releases next week, including July inflation, May trade figures, and Q2 GDP. The dollar itself remained soft, pressured by the Fed's cautious stance and suspected Japanese intervention to support the yen. Even so, the rupiah slipped about 0.5% on the week, extending prior weakness and leaving it on course for a fifth straight monthly drop. The currency remained under pressure amid uncertainty over the future monetary policy following Perry Warjiyo's sudden exit as central bank governor, despite Bank Indonesia's recent pledge to intensify rupiah stabilisation efforts through a broader policy mix beyond interest rates. Analysts caution that if President Prabowo's choice of successor leans more on political loyalty than technocratic credibility, fears of "fiscal dominance" could deepen, further eroding investor confidence.

title: Poland Inflation Rate Rises in July
summary: The annual inflation rate in Poland accelerated to 3.0% year-on-year in July 2026 from 2.5% in the previous month, according to preliminary estimates. The increase was mainly driven by faster price growth for fuels and lubricants for private means of transport (15.8%), while inflation for electricity, gas, and other fuels also accelerated to 4.0%. Meanwhile, prices for food and non-alcoholic beverages declined by 0.4%. On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.8% in July, rebounding from a 0.5% decline in June and returning to growth after posting declines in the previous two months.

title: Austria Inflation Rate Eases to 5-Month Low
summary: Austria’s annual inflation rate eased to 2.7% in July 2026 from 3.2% in the previous month, preliminary estimates showed. This marked the lowest reading since February, largely driven by lower food prices. Food, alcohol, and tobacco prices fell 0.1% year-on-year, down from a 1.5% increase in June, partly reflecting the reduction in VAT on basic foodstuffs from 10% to 4.9% effective July 2026. Price growth for manufactured goods also slowed to 0.8% from 1.1%, while services remained the main driver of inflation, with prices rising 4.4%, unchanged from June. In contrast, energy price growth accelerated slightly to 5.7% from 5.4%, as fuel and heating oil prices increased more strongly in the second half of July. On a monthly basis, consumer prices declined 0.1% in July, following a flat reading in June.

title: European Stocks Rise to Record High
summary: The STOXX 50 gained 1.1% and the STOXX 600 advanced 0.9% to hit record levels on Friday, tracking a global rally in technology shares as investors renewed their enthusiasm for AI-related stocks. Fresh corporate earnings and lower oil prices also supported market sentiment. ASML climbed 3.4%, Infineon surged 6.8%, STMicroelectronics went up 4.1% and Siemens Energy gained 3.6%. NatWest rose 3.8% after reporting a stronger-than-expected 29% increase in pre-tax profit, while Saint-Gobain advanced 4.8% after posting an acceleration in second-quarter sales growth. Engie added 4.2% after posting a 3.3% rise in earnings and Credit Agricole rose 3.6% after reporting higher profit for Q2. Worldline soared nearly 19% after its earnings report. In contrast, Vivendi plunged more than 13% to bottom the STOXX 600. On the week, the STOXX 50 is up 1%, while the STOXX 600 has gained 0.9%. For July, the STOXX 50 has risen 0.2%, while the STOXX 600 has advanced 1.3%.

title: European Stocks Rise
summary: European stocks traded higher on Friday, with the STOXX 50 gaining 1.1% and the STOXX 600 advancing 0.9%, tracking a global rally in technology shares as investors renewed their enthusiasm for AI-related stocks. Fresh corporate earnings and lower oil prices also supported market sentiment. ASML climbed 3.4%, Infineon surged 6.8%, STMicroelectronics went up 4.1% and Siemens Energy gained 3.6%. NatWest rose 3.8% after reporting a stronger-than-expected 29% increase in pre-tax profit, while Saint-Gobain advanced 4.8% after posting an acceleration in second-quarter sales growth. Engie added 4.2% after posting a 3.3% rise in earnings and Credit Agricole rose 3.6% after reporting higher profit for Q2. Worldline soared nearly 19% after its earnings report. In contrast, Vivendi plunged more than 13% to bottom the STOXX 600. On the week, the STOXX 50 is up 1%, while the STOXX 600 has gained 0.9%. For July, the STOXX 50 has risen 0.2%, while the STOXX 600 has advanced 1.3%.

title: Energy Commodities Updates: Crude Oil WTI Falls by 1.65%
summary: Top commodity losers are Crude Oil WTI (-1.65%), Gasoline (-1.44%) and Brent Crude Oil (-1.31%).

title: Bund Yield Eases but Posts Strongest Monthly Gain Since March
summary: Germany's 10-year Bund yield edged lower to 3.15% on Friday, tracking a decline in oil prices as energy supplies continued to move through key maritime routes despite limited progress in US-Iran talks. Even so, the benchmark yield gained 28 basis points in July, its largest monthly increase since March, while the two-year Bund yield climbed more than 22 basis points, as growing concerns over the longer-term inflationary impact of the Middle East conflict prompted investors to increase bets on further ECB rate hikes. Money markets now fully price the European Central Bank's deposit rate at 2.75% by early 2027 following stronger-than-expected GDP data and persistent inflationary pressures across the euro area. After raising interest rates in June and leaving them unchanged in July, the ECB is now expected to deliver two additional rate hikes, with the first potentially coming as early as September.

title: Metals Commodities Updates: Titanium Drops by 2.20%
summary: Top commodity losers are Titanium (-2.20%), Lithium Carbonate (-2.05%), Silver (-1.46%) and Gold (-0.97%). Gains are led by Copper (0.61%).

title: Telecom Italia Stock Price Hits 7-week Low
summary: Telecom Italia shares decreased to 7.31 EUR, the lowest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Telecom Italia lost 10.07%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 1713.43%.

title: Euro Heads for Monthly Gain on Strong Eurozone Data
summary: The euro held above $1.15, hovering near its highest level since June 16 and on track for a monthly gain of 0.8%, supported by stronger-than-expected eurozone economic data. The bloc's economy expanded by 0.4% in the Q2, surpassing forecasts of 0.2% and marking its fastest growth since early 2025. Meanwhile, inflation accelerated across the euro area's largest economies in July, reinforcing concerns that higher energy costs could spill over into services and core prices. As a result, markets fully priced in the European Central Bank's deposit rate reaching 2.75% by early 2027, implying two additional rate hikes, with the first potentially as soon as September. In the US, the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged this week, while three FOMC members dissented in favor of a rate hike. Markets now assign around a 65% probability of a September hike. Meanwhile, oil prices fell, as energy shipments continued through key maritime routes despite limited progress in US-Iran talks.

title: Philippines Business Confidence Recovers in June
summary: The Business Confidence Index in the Philippines improved sharply to 0.0 in June 2026 from -25.2 in the previous month. The turnaround was driven by expectations of higher consumer spending with the start of the new academic year, alongside lower oil prices and energy costs. Notable improvements in the volume of business activity (8.3 vs -4.5 in May), total orders booked (5.4 vs -2.2), and access to credit (-5.7 vs -7.3), while average capacity utilization increased (73.9% vs 70.5%). However, firms continued to report weak financial conditions, with the financial condition remaining negative at -26.8 from -25.7 in the previous month. Looking ahead, the three-month business outlook strengthened to 18.8 from 0.6, while one-year confidence rose to 42.4 from 27.8, supported by expectations of stronger consumer demand, easing inflation, improved economic conditions, and a possible resolution of the Middle East conflict.

title: FTSE 100 Posts Best Month Since February
summary: The FTSE 100 climbed more than 0.5% on Friday to a fresh record high near 10,970, putting the index on track for a weekly gain of around 2.2% and a monthly advance of roughly 4.5%, its strongest performance since February. Investors continued to monitor weaker oil prices and renewed volatility in semiconductor stocks. NatWest jumped nearly 4% after raising its full-year guidance and announcing plans for a share buyback alongside its 2026 annual results. J Sainsbury gained more than 3% after agreeing to sell its Argos business to Swift Partners for at least £120 million. On the downside, Pearson fell almost 4% despite reaffirming its outlook, while IG Group dropped over 5% after announcing a deal worth up to $1.3 billion to acquire US sports prediction platform Underdog. IAG lost around 1.6% after missing revenue estimates and warning of higher fuel costs and prolonged Middle East route suspensions.

title: Taiwan Q2 GDP Growth Loses Momentum
summary: Taiwan’s economy expanded 12.92% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, beating market expectations of 10.8% but slowing from a multi-decade high of 14.55% in the previous quarter, preliminary estimates showed. The latest reading marked the weakest economic growth since Q3 2025, as external demand lost momentum, with exports of goods and services growth easing to 21.64% from 35.76% in Q1, while imports slowed to 18.27% from 26.34%. Meanwhile, domestic demand strengthened, supported by firmer household consumption, which rose to 5.88% from 4.74% previously, and gross capital formation, which accelerated to 15.14% from 5.92%. In contrast, government spending moderated to 3.22% from 4.06%. On a seasonally adjusted quarterly basis, Taiwan’s economy grew 2.39% in Q2 2026, accelerating from 1.69% growth in the first quarter.

title: Italy Manufacturing Confidence at 2023-Highs
summary: Italy's manufacturing confidence indicator rose to 89.6 in July 2026, the highest level since June 2023, up from 88.6 in the previous month, marking a broad-based improvement in business sentiment. Firms reported a less negative assessment of both total orders (-16.5 vs -19.3), reflecting improvements in sentiment of foreign orders (-21.9 vs -24.5). Meanwhile, views on current production strengthened slightly (-15.0 vs -15.7), although still in negative territory, alongside a further buildup in inventories (2.7 vs 1.4). Looking ahead, production expectations improved (3.5 vs 1.8), while inflation expectations eased markedly (15.3 vs 22.0), pointing to softer cost pressures. Labor market sentiment also rebounded sharply, with the employment indicator rising to 4.4 from -1.8. Meanwhile, Italy's overall business confidence edged up to 95.6 from 95.3, supported by stronger sentiment in market services, and retail trade, while confidence in the construction sector weakened.

title: Turkey Tourist Arrivals Down 4.02% in June
summary: The number of foreign visitors to Turkey dropped by 4.02% year-on-year to 5.54 million in June 2026, following a 3.58% fall in the previous month. Among the five largest source markets, arrivals declined from Germany (-11.30%), the United Kingdom (-13.87%), and Poland (-3.06%), while increased from Russia (2.13%) and Iran (68.17%). By region, Europe remained the biggest source of foreign visitors, accounting for 49.28% of total arrivals, followed by Asia (13.84%), Africa (2.21%), and the Americas (0.78%). Antalya and Istanbul remained the country's most popular destinations, attracting 36.13% and 29.94% of all foreign visitors, respectively. In the first half of 2026, total foreign arrivals fell 2.96% from a year earlier to 20.77 million.

title: Crypto Updates: Ether Depreciates by 1.34%
summary: Top crypto losers are Ether (-1.34%) and Bitcoin (-1.25%).

title: German Unemployment Rate Rises to 6.4%
summary: Germany's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 6.4% in July 2026 from 6.3% in June, exceeding market expectations of 6.3%. The number of unemployed increased by slightly more than expected, rising by 6,000 to 2.99 million, just below the politically significant 3 million threshold. On a non-seasonally adjusted basis, unemployment climbed above 3 million. The labor market has continued to weaken with a lag following the geopolitical shock of the Iran war, which began in February. Adding to the pressure, inflation accelerated to 2.8% in July as higher energy prices filtered through the economy. Although Germany's second-quarter GDP growth exceeded expectations, the outlook remains clouded by renewed US-Iran hostilities, which could keep energy prices elevated, reinforce expectations of tighter ECB policy, and weigh on investment and consumer spending.

title: Spain Current Account Surplus Narrows in May
summary: Spain's current account surplus narrowed to EUR 1.84 billion in May 2026 from EUR 6.37 billion in the same month last year. The goods and services surplus fell to EUR 5.74 billion from EUR 8.42 billion. Tourism revenues, however, rose to EUR 7.6 million from EUR 6.9 billion a year earlier. Also, the primary and secondary income deficit widened to EUR 3.90 billion from EUR 2.05 billion.

title: Italy Consumer Morale Hits 5-Month High
summary: The consumer confidence index in Italy rose to 94.2 in July 2026 from 92.4 in the previous month, exceeding market expectations of 92.5. It marked the highest reading since February 2025, as all main components strengthened, led by a broad-based rise in expectations. The economic climate sub-index increased to 90.9 from 87.6 in June, while the future climate advanced to 89.8 from 87.4, reflecting a more favorable outlook for the broader economy. The personal climate climbed to 95.4 from 94.2, while the current climate edged higher to 97.4 from 96.2.

title: Slovenia Inflation Rate Slows in July
summary: The annual inflation rate in Slovakia slowed to 2.9% in July 2026, easing to the lowest level since March, down from 3.6% in the previous month, reflecting softer price pressures for both goods (2.0% vs 2.9%) and services (4.6% vs 5.0%). Food prices fell 0.4% after rising 0.5% in June, while inflation eased for housing and utilities (4.7% vs 4.9%), transport (2.6% vs 4.7%), healthcare (2.1% vs 5.1%), information and communication (2.8% vs 3.0%), and education services (3.1% vs 3.2%). Restaurant and hotel prices rose at an unchanged pace of 2.7%. Meanwhile, inflation accelerated for recreation, sports and culture (6.3% vs 4.8%), clothing and footwear (0.9% vs 0.0%), furnishings and household equipment (1.3% vs 0.6%), and insurance and financial services (2.5% vs 2.2%). On a monthly basis, consumer prices fell 0.1% in July, the first monthly decline since January, following a 0.9% increase in June. Harmonised inflation slowed to 3% in July from 3.7% in the prior month.

title: Portugal Inflation Eases to 3.0%, but Core Price Pressures Pick Up
summary: Portugal's annual inflation rate edged down to 3.0% in July 2026, easing for a third consecutive month, according to a preliminary estimate. The slowdown was driven by softer energy inflation, which eased to 8.7% from 9.1%, and slower food price growth, with unprocessed food inflation falling to 3.7% from 5.1%. However, underlying price pressures strengthened, as core inflation, which excludes energy and unprocessed food, rose to 2.6% from 2.5%. Meanwhile, the EU-harmonized inflation rate remained unchanged at 3.1%, hovering near its highest level in two years and staying well above the European Central Bank's 2.0% target.

title: Hong Kong GDP Grows 4.3% in Q2
summary: Hong Kong’s economy expanded 4.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, easing from 5.9% growth in the previous quarter and coming in slightly below expectations of 4.8%, according to preliminary estimates. Growth slowed in private consumption expenditure (2.9% vs. 4.9% in Q1) and government consumption expenditure (0.5% vs. 2.8%). Gross fixed capital formation also lost momentum, increasing 4.6% compared with an 18.3% rise in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, external demand remained a key driver of growth, with exports of goods rising to 28.8% from 23.8%, while imports of goods rose at a slightly slower pace of 29.3% after 29.9% in Q1. On a seasonally adjusted quarterly basis, GDP contracted 0.6% in Q2, reversing a 2.9% expansion in the preceding quarter and marking the first quarterly decline since the third quarter of 2022.

title: FX Updates: Japanese Yen Rises by 0.54%
summary: Top currency gainers are Japanese Yen (0.54%) and Brazilian Real (0.26%). Biggest loser is South Korean Won (-0.52%). Meanwhile, Dollar Index, Euro and British Pound were little changed.

title: Macau Q2 GDP Growth Slows Sharply
summary: Macau’s economy grew by 0.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, easing sharply from a 7.1% expansion in the previous quarter, according to preliminary estimates. Despite the slowdown, it marked the fifth consecutive quarter of economic growth, driven largely by a 7.2% increase in services exports amid a 13.9% year-on-year surge in visitor arrivals. On the domestic front, private consumption expenditure continued to grow steadily, rising 2.8% from a year earlier. Meanwhile, government spending fell 4.8%, while gross fixed capital formation declined sharply by 21.9%.

title: Macau Jobless Rate Edges Up to 1.9%
summary: Macau’s unemployment rate edged up by 1.9% in June 2026, following a 1.8% increase in the previous two months. The number of unemployed decreased by 300 month-on-month to 6.8 thousand, while employment rose by 2,300 to 376.4 thousand. The labour force participation rate also increased to 66.8% from 66.3% a month earlier, with the labour force rising by 2,800 to 383.6 thousand. Participation was lower among women (60.0%) than among men (64.1%). By industry, gaming accounted for the largest share of employed residents (63.2%), followed by wholesale and retail trade (36.1%), real estate and business activities (24.6%), accommodation and food industries (20.2%), and transport and storage (16.7%).

title: Italian Inflation Softens as Expected
summary: The annual inflation rate in Italy eased to 2.8% in July of 2026 from 3% in the previous month, aligned with the median market consensus, according to a preliminary estimate. It was the second pullback since the rate surged to an over-two-year high of 3.2% in May, reflecting some softening as the temporary resumption of energy exports from the Middle East brought relief to wholesale prices in the period. Non-regulated energy inflation, which are more sensitive to swings in global benchmarks, eased to 10.6% from 13.3% in June. Prices also slowed for fresh food (3.8% vs 4.4%) and broad services (1.8% vs 2.5%). In turn, prices rebounded for non-fresh food (0.2% vs -0.2%) and rose faster for regulated energy (14.9% vs 9.2%) and transportation services (1.6% vs 1.1%). Core inflation, which excludes energy and fresh food prices due to their often exogenous price swings, eased to 1.8% from 1.9%).

title: Eurozone Inflation Climbs to 2.9% in July
summary: Eurozone annual inflation accelerated to 2.9% in July 2026, in line with market expectations, up from 2.8% in June and remaining well above the European Central Bank's 2.0% target, according to preliminary estimates. The increase was largely driven by a renewed surge in energy prices, with energy inflation accelerating to 10.0% from 8.5% as hostilities between the US and Iran resumed. Underlying price pressures also strengthened. Services inflation edged up to 3.3% from 3.2%, while inflation for non-energy industrial goods rose to 0.9% from 0.7%. In contrast, food, alcohol, and tobacco inflation eased to 1.2% from 1.5%. The core inflation rate, which excludes energy and food, increased to 2.5% from 2.4%. Among the euro area's largest economies, inflation accelerated in Germany (2.8% vs. 2.4%), France (2.4% vs. 2.0%), Spain (3.8% vs. 3.6%), and the Netherlands (2.9% vs. 2.5%), while easing slightly in Italy (2.9% vs. 3.0%).

title: Croatia Inflation Rate Eases to 5-Month Low
summary: The inflation rate in Croatia eased to 3.9% year-on-year in July 2026 from 4.5% in the previous month, marking the lowest reading since February, according to a preliminary estimate. Prices for non-food industrial goods excluding energy declined 1.1% year-on-year, contributing to the overall moderation in inflation. In contrast, energy costs climbed 12.2%, reflecting ongoing pressures associated with the Middle East conflict. Services prices also continued to rise strongly, increasing 8.5%, while food, beverages, and tobacco prices advanced 0.5%. On a monthly basis, consumer prices fell 0.2% in July, following a 0.4% decline in June, extending the downward trend for the third consecutive month, albeit at a softer pace.

title: Greece Retail Sales Growth at One-Year High
summary: Retail sales in Greece rose by 6.8% year-on-year in May 2026, rebounding from 0.3% decline in the previous month, highest reading since April 2025. The recovery was supported by stronger performance across major segments, with sales of non-food products excluding automotive fuel surging (7.7% vs -1.1% in April). Food sales also accelerated (7.7% vs 2.9%), while automotive fuel sales declined at a slower pace (-0.6% vs -6.6%). Among the major retail categories, growth accelerated in furniture, electrical equipment, and household goods (10.6% vs 5.3%), pharmaceutical products and cosmetics (8.4% vs 2.6%), food, beverages, and tobacco (7.9% vs 3.3%), and supermarkets (6.9% vs 1.9%). Meanwhile, clothing and footwear (8.6% vs -6.3%), department stores (5.8% vs -3.9%) rebounded, while automotive fuel remained in contraction, albeit at a much slower pace (-0.6% vs -6.6%). On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, retail activity rose 3.3% in May.

title: Pound Holds Near Two-Week High as Markets Reassess BoE Rate Path
summary: The pound traded around $1.345, close to its strongest level in nearly two weeks, and was heading for a monthly gain of more than 1% against the dollar, its best monthly performance since April. Sterling was supported by investors reassessing the Bank of England’s July decision and by fading political uncertainty in the UK, as the country welcomed its seventh prime minister in a decade, with the new government pledging to adhere to fiscal rules. The BoE voted 6-3 to keep interest rates unchanged, with three policymakers favoring a rate hike compared with expectations for a 7-2 split. However, Governor Andrew Bailey pushed back against speculation of an imminent tightening cycle, saying the disinflation process remains intact, while some officials noted rate cuts could return to focus if the Iran conflict ends. Markets are now pricing in just one rate hike by the end of the year, while renewed US-Iran hostilities continue to add uncertainty to the economic outlook.

title: Belgium Producer Inflation Slows
summary: Belgium's producer price inflation eased to 9.1% year-on-year in June 2026 from 9.7% in the previous month, as domestic price pressures softened (8.3% vs 9.1%), partly offset by faster inflation in foreign markets (11.0% vs 8.2%). By sector, producer inflation slowed for manufacturing (9.0% vs 10.3%) but accelerated for mining and quarrying (2.3% vs 1.9%) and electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply (11.5% vs 4.3%), while remaining unchanged for water supply, sewage, waste management and remediation activities (4.2%). Energy inflation eased sharply to 16.6% from 24.4%. Meanwhile, producer prices fell at a slower pace for consumer goods (-1.3% vs -2.2%), reflecting softer deflation for non-durable goods (-1.6% vs -2.4%), while inflation accelerated for intermediate goods (17.2% vs 15.7%) and durable consumer goods (4.7% vs 4.1%). On a monthly basis, producer prices declined 1.1% in June, following a 0.8% increase in May.

title: Macau Trade Deficit Widens in June
summary: Macau’s trade deficit widened to MOP 10.9 billion in June 2026 from MOP 8.8 billion in the same month a year earlier. Imports rose 24.4% year-on-year to MOP 12.1 billion, driven by stronger purchases of gold and jewellery (79.1%) and mobile phones (46.8%), while imports of food and beverages declined 13.4%. During the January–June period, imports increased notably from China (40.8%), France (10.9%), Italy (9.6%), Hong Kong (7.1%), and Japan (5.8%). Meanwhile, exports climbed 32.7% to MOP 1.3 billion, supported by higher re-exports of diamonds and diamond jewellery (47.3%) as well as domestic exports of copper and related articles (16.5%), while pharmaceutical products and organic chemicals fell by 12.3%. During the January–June period, exports also grew to Hong Kong (72.7%), China (10.9%), and the United States (1.6%). In the first half of 2026, Macau recorded a cumulative trade deficit of MOP 66.1 billion, compared with MOP 46.1 billion in the same period a year earlier.

title: UK Gilt Yields Ease but Post Steep Monthly Rise in July
summary: UK 10-year gilt yields edged lower to 4.99% on Friday, tracking a decline in oil prices as energy flows continued through key maritime routes despite limited progress in US-Iran talks. Still, the benchmark yield rose 23 basis points in July, as elevated oil prices fueled concerns over the longer-term inflation impact of the Middle East conflict and boosted expectations for a tighter Bank of England policy stance. The gilt market was also supported by fading political uncertainty, with the UK welcoming its seventh prime minister in a decade and the new government pledging to adhere to fiscal rules. On Thursday, the BoE voted 6-3 to keep rates unchanged in July, with three policymakers favoring a hike against expectations for a 7-2 split. However, Governor Andrew Bailey pushed back against expectations of an imminent tightening cycle, while some officials noted rate cuts could return to focus if the Iran conflict ends. Markets now price in one rate hike by year-end.

title: Sri Lanka Producer Inflation Slows in June
summary: Producer prices in Sri Lanka rose by 1.3% year-on-year in June 2026, easing from an upwardly revised 3.3% rise in the previous month. Agricultural producer prices fell at a faster pace (-10.7% vs -9.5% in May), mainly due to weaker prices for perennial and non-perennial crops. Meanwhile, electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply prices accelerated (15.8% vs 13.4%), while water collection, treatment and supply also recorded faster growth (5.9% vs 5.7%). Manufacturing inflation increased further (3.6% vs 3.2%), supported by higher costs of chemical products, non-metallic mineral products, other transport equipment, and food products. On a monthly basis, producer prices declined 1.2% in June, reversing a 1.6% increase in the previous month.

title: North Macedonia Retail Sales Drop in June
summary: North Macedonia's retail sales fell 1.0% year-on-year in June 2026, marking the first annual decline since September 2025 and reversing from a 7.3% increase in May. The downturn was driven by a 4.2% drop in sales of food, beverages and tobacco, following a 9.1% rise in the previous month, while sales growth of automotive fuels also slowed sharply to 2.5% from 14.7%, contributing to a 1.1% decline in retail trade excluding automotive fuel, after a 6.2% increase in May. Meanwhile, sales of non-food products excluding fuel continued to grow, although at a slightly slower pace of 1.4%, compared with 1.6% in the previous month.

title: Portugal Industrial Production Declines Again in June
summary: Portugal’s industrial production fell 0.7% year-on-year in June 2026, following a revised 1.6% decline in May as the contraction in energy output eased sharply (-1.0% vs. -9.7%). However, production remained weak across most sectors, with declines in durable goods (-1.0%), non-durable goods (-2.5%), and capital goods (-2.9%). In contrast, intermediate goods output accelerated, rising 2.2% after a 0.9% increase in May. On a monthly basis, industrial activity dropped 3.8% in June, marking its largest decline in a year.

title: Sri Lanka Inflation Rate Hits Over 3-Year High
summary: The inflation rate in Colombo, Sri Lanka’s capital, rose to 7.3% in July 2026 from 6.8% in the previous month, well above market expectations of 6.7%. This marked the highest reading since June 2023, as food inflation accelerated to a more than three-year high of 6.3% from 3.6% in June, while non-food prices remained elevated but eased to 7.8% from 8.4%. Prices increased faster for furnishing and equipment (5.4% vs 4.5% in June), communication (0.5% vs 0.3%), education (7.2% vs 6.5%), restaurants and hotels (10.6% vs 10.3%), and miscellaneous goods and services (6.2% vs 5.8%). Meanwhile, inflation slowed for transport (17.2% vs 18.7%), clothing and footwear (0.8% vs 1.3%), housing and utilities (5.4% vs 6.3%), and health (3.0% vs 4.2%). Costs were flat for alcoholic beverages and tobacco after a 1.7% increase, while prices for recreation and culture declined further (-2.1% vs -1.4%). On a monthly basis, consumer prices moderated to 0.2% in July from 2.1% in the previous month.

title: North Macedonia Industrial Output Rebounds in June
summary: North Macedonia’s industrial production increased 6.5% year-on-year in June 2026, rebounding from a 2.0% decline in May. Manufacturing output returned to growth (7.9% vs. -2.6% in May). In contrast, mining and quarrying output declined further (-3.8% vs. -3.6%), and ouput in electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply fell (-8.2% vs 6.1%). By industrial grouping, growth accelerated for intermediate goods excluding energy (11.7% vs. 3.4%), while output rebounded for capital goods (8.6% vs. -3.3%), durable consumer goods (8.6% vs. -1.1%), and non-durable consumer goods (2.0% vs. -8.4%). Meanwhile, energy production contracted sharply (-11.1% vs. 6.5%). In the first half of 2026, industrial output rose 0.9% compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.

title: India Fiscal Deficit Widens
summary: India's fiscal deficit surged to INR 3.1 trillion in the first quarter of FY2027 from INR 280 billion in the corresponding period of the previous year. This was equivalent to 28.7% of the current budget estimate, which is commonly depleted toward the end of the fiscal year, compared to 26.7% in the previous year. As a net energy importer, the country is grappling with rising fuel subsidy costs due to elevated oil prices linked to the ongoing Middle East conflict. Total expenditure surged 11.0% year-on-year to INR 13.5 trillion (25.4% of budgeted amount), while total receipts rose by 11.5 to INR 10-5 trillion (28.7% of the budgeted amount).

title: US Futures Extend Rebound
summary: Futures tracking US equity indices extended yesterday's rebound amid another strong session for chip producers and optimistic corporate results. Contract for the S&P 500 and the Dow were around 0.5% higher, while the Nasdaq 100 rose over 1%. Amazon surged over 10% premarket after reporting an acceleration in cloud-computing revenue for a fifth quarter, easing concerns that soaring AI spending would not produce returns. The rhetoric was aligned with a second session of gains for chip producers as markets grappled with concerns that spending could slow on AI infrastructure against the large potential upside on the trade. Micron and Sandisk were each 5% higher, set to erase the selloff from earlier in the week. In turn, Apple slipped 7% as the shortage for chips raised costs and dented production. Meanwhile, Exxon and Chevron were mixed after their earnings, unveiling the magnitude of the benefit from soaring energy costs from the Middle East-war.

title: Brazil Budget Deficit Widens More Than Expected
summary: The Brazilian government posted a nominal budget deficit of BRL 166 billion in June 2026, widening from BRL 108.1 billion in the same month a year earlier and exceeding market expectations of a BRL 133.2 billion shortfall. The federal government recorded a BRL 47.2 billion deficit, while regional governments posted a BRL 6.6 billion deficit and state-owned companies registered a BRL 5.5 billion shortfall. Meanwhile, gross government debt rose to 81.9% of GDP in July, the highest level since October 2021, up from 81.1% in the previous month and above market forecasts of 81.5%. Over the 12 months through July, the nominal public sector deficit widened to 1.19% of GDP from 1.14% in the previous month.

title: Brazil Producer Prices Fall the Most in a Year
summary: Brazil's producer prices fell 0.77% month-over-month in June 2026, following a 0.30% decline in May and marking the sharpest monthly drop in a year. The decrease was driven mainly by the extractive industries, where producer prices plunged 11.85% as crude oil, iron ore, and natural gas prices declined after geopolitical tensions in the Middle East eased and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz increased. Other major negative contributors included chemicals (-2.74%) and oil refining and biofuels (-2.30%). Among major economic categories, intermediate goods fell 1.7% and were the main drag on the index, while capital goods rose 1.02% and consumer goods increased 0.25%. Producer prices rose 3.99% in the first half of 2026 and were up 2.51% from a year earlier.

title: South Africa Trade Surplus Widens in June
summary: South Africa's trade surplus widened to ZAR 17.75 billion in June 2026 from an upwardly revised ZAR 4.44 billion in the previous month, as exports increased while imports declined. Exports rose 4.3% to ZAR 193.6 billion, driven by higher shipments of vehicles and transport equipment (16%), chemical products (6%), prepared foodstuffs (6%), and precious metals and stones (2%). Meanwhile, imports fell 2.9% to ZAR 175.8 billion, reflecting lower purchases of mineral products (-15%), vehicles and transport equipment (-12%), and original equipment components (-6%). Despite the monthly improvement, the trade surplus was smaller than the ZAR 20.96 billion surplus recorded in the same month a year earlier.

title: US Employment Costs Slightly Above Forecasts
summary: Compensation costs for civilian workers in the United States rose by 0.9% in the second quarter of 2026, the same as in the previous period, slightly above forecasts of a 0.8% rise. Wages and salaries increased 0.9% (vs 0.8% in Q1) and benefits rose at a faster pace of 1% (vs 1.2%). Compensation costs for private industry workers grew 0.9%, the same as in Q1, and for state and local government workers grew 1%, also the same as in Q1. On an annual basis, employment cost growth remained unchanged from the last period at 3.4%.

title: Canada GDP Expands Further
summary: The Canadian GDP is expected to have grown by 0.2% from the previous month in June of 2026, translating to a 0.8% expansion in the second quarter. The preliminary data indicated higher output for wholesale, finance and insurance, and retail trade. These offset declines for utilities and agriculture. Richer data showed that the GDP expanded by 0.3% in May, reflecting some resilience despite the inflationary pressure from higher energy prices in the period due to the war in Iran. Goods producing industries expanded by 0.6% amid as higher oil and gas prices lifted mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction output by 1%. Meanwhile, services expanded by 0.2%, as a 0.4% growth rate in real estate and 0.3% jump in retail trade offset a 0.4% contraction in wholesale trade.

title: TSX Futures Muted as Markets Assess GDP and Earnings
summary: Futures tracking the S&P/TSX Composite Index were little changed on Friday as investors assessed another round of corporate earnings and Canada's May GDP report. Fairfax Financial and Cameco reported revenue above expectations, although both missed EPS forecasts. Enbridge beat estimates for second-quarter adjusted profit. Imperial Oil reported quarterly earnings above expectations as profit doubled on higher crude prices and stronger refining margins. On the data front, Canada's economy expanded 0.3% in May, the second consecutive monthly increase and slightly above forecasts of 0.2%, reinforcing the BoC's view that the economy is adjusting to recent shocks. Meanwhile, gold prices fell as a stronger US dollar weighed on mining stocks. Oil prices extended gains, supporting energy shares but fueling inflation concerns.

title: Chile Jobless Rate Steady at 2021-Highs
summary: Chile's unemployment rate stood at 9.4% in the April-June 2026 period, unchanged from the previous rolling quarter and in line with market expectations. The reading remained at its highest level since the quarter ending June 2021. The labor force increased 1.5% year-on-year, while the labor force participation rate edged down to 62.3% from 62.4%, as the number of unemployed eased slightly to 980 thousand. Meanwhile, employment rose 0.9% from a year earlier to 9.403 million, although the employment rate edged down to 56.4% from 56.5% in the previous period. Job creation was primarily driven by gains in transportation (6.8%), administrative and support service activities (12.9%), and human health activities (5.1%).

title: Chile Industrial Production Rebounds in June
summary: Chile's industrial production rose 1.3% year-on-year in June 2026, rebounding from a 7.5% decline in May and marking the first expansion in nine months. The recovery was driven by a 6% increase in mining output, as metallic mining rose 4.6%, non-metallic mining advanced 14.5%, and energy resources production increased 4.3%. Copper production was up 5.1% from a year earlier. Utilities output also grew 2.4%, led by a 3.5% increase in electricity generation, supported by higher output from coal and coal-petcoke power plants. In contrast, manufacturing output contracted 3.2%, mainly due to an 8.1% decline in food production. On a monthly basis, industrial production increased 1.6%.

title: Chile Copper Output Rebounds in June
summary: Chile's copper production rose 5.1% year-on-year to 447,294 metric tons in June 2026, rebounding from a 12.9% decline in May. The increase was driven by higher ore processing at the country's major mining companies. The recovery in Chile, the world's largest copper producer, helped ease concerns over tightening global copper supply. Meanwhile, Chile's Mining Production Index rose 6% from a year earlier, supported by a 4.6% increase in metallic mining, a 14.5% rise in non-metallic mining, and a 4.3% gain in energy resources production.

title: Amazon Stock Price Hits 8-week High
summary: Amazon shares increased to 264.17 USD, the highest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Amazon gained 8.86%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 12.39%.

title: Apple Stock Price Hits 4-week Low
summary: Apple shares decreased to 301.86 USD, the lowest since July 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Apple gained 3.31%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 46.52%.

title: T-Mobile Us Stock Price Hits 4-week Low
summary: T-Mobile Us shares decreased to 169.86 USD, the lowest since July 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, T-Mobile Us lost 1.69%, and in the last 12 months, it decreased 28.64%.

title: US Stocks Rebound on Friday
summary: Futures tracking US equity indices extended yesterday's rebound amid another strong session for chip producers and optimistic corporate results. Contract for the S&P 500 and the Dow were around 0.3% higher, while the Nasdaq 100 rose nearly 1%. Amazon surged over 10% premarket after reporting an acceleration in cloud-computing revenue for a fifth quarter, easing concerns that soaring AI spending would not produce returns. The rhetoric was aligned with a second session of gains for chip producers as markets grappled with concerns that spending could slow on AI infrastructure against the large potential upside on the trade. Micron and Sandisk gained, erasing the selloff from the week, while AMD added 4% and Nvidia gained 3%. In turn, Apple slipped 7% as the shortage for chips raised costs and dented production. Meanwhile, Exxon and Chevron were mixed after their earnings, unveiling the magnitude of the benefit from soaring energy costs from the Middle East-war.

title: Eli Lilly Stock Price Hits 5-week Low
summary: Eli Lilly shares decreased to 1134.00 USD, the lowest since June 2026. Over the past 4 weeks, Eli Lilly lost 4.5%, and in the last 12 months, it increased 53.78%.

title: US 10 Year Treasury Yield Back to 2025-Highs
summary: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note rose to 4.71% on Friday, returning to its highest level since January 2025, as investors weighed hawkish remarks from Fed policymakers that reinforced the case for higher interest rates to curb inflation. Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said he would prefer smaller rate hikes now rather than waiting, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned that the longer inflation remains elevated, the more difficult and costly it will be to bring it back to target. Both were among the three FOMC members who dissented at this week's meeting, voting in favor of a 25bps rate hike, although the Fed ultimately left the federal funds rate unchanged. Even so, investors' expectations for a rate hike at the next policy meeting in September eased after Governor Kevin Warsh offered little guidance on the future path of monetary policy, although markets continue to price in roughly a two-thirds probability of a 25bps increase.

title: Euro Ends Month Steady as Strong Data Counters Geopolitical Tensions
summary: The euro traded around $1.145, ending the month little changed against the US dollar as stronger-than-expected eurozone data offset mounting geopolitical tensions. The eurozone economy grew 0.4% in the second quarter, beating forecasts of 0.2% and marking its strongest expansion since early 2025. Meanwhile, annual inflation accelerated to 2.9% in July, with core and services inflation also strengthening. The data reinforced expectations for further ECB tightening, with markets fully pricing in the deposit rate reaching 2.75% by early 2027, implying two additional rate hikes, the first potentially in September. In the US, the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, although three FOMC members dissented in favor of a rate hike. Markets now assign about a 65% probability of a September increase. Meanwhile, oil prices jumped more than 20% this month after renewed US-Iran strikes, fueling concerns over energy supplies and inflation.

title: US Consumer Sentiment Revised Higher to Five-Month High
summary: The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index was revised higher to 55.2 in July 2026 from a preliminary reading of 54.0, reaching its highest level since February, before the US-Iran conflict drove gas prices higher. Sentiment improved across all income, age, education, wealth, and political groups. Consumers' five-year outlook for business conditions climbed to a 12-month high, though it remained well below its historical average. Despite the improvement, overall sentiment was still 11% lower than a year earlier, reflecting continued concerns over elevated prices and the lasting effects of several years of high inflation. Year-ahead inflation expectations eased to 4.2% from 4.6% in June, while long-run expectations held steady at 3.3%. Interviews for the survey were conducted between June 23 and July 27.

title: US 1-Year Inflation Expectations Confirmed at 4.2%
summary: Year-ahead inflation expectations in the United States, as measured by the University of Michigan survey, fell for a second consecutive month to 4.2% in July 2026, the lowest level since March, down from 4.6% in June and in line with the preliminary estimate. Even so, expectations remained well above the 3.4% recorded in February, before the outbreak of the Iran conflict, and above all readings seen throughout 2024. Meanwhile, the five-year inflation outlook stood at 3.3% in July, matching both June's reading and the preliminary estimate. Nevertheless, it remained slightly above the 2.8%-3.2% range that prevailed throughout 2024.

title: TSX Slips as Miners Losses Weigh
summary: The S&P/TSX Composite Index edged lower to below 35,500 on Friday, weighed down by losses in mining stocks. Gold prices fell amid a sharp rebound for long-term Treasury yields. Agnico Eagle was down more than 3%, while Barrick and WPM lost over 2% each. Software stocks also weakened, with Shopify and Constellation Software down about 0.5%. Meanwhile, Fairfax Financial (-2%) and Cameco (-0.1%) reported revenue above expectations, but both missed EPS forecasts. Enbridge slipped more than 0.5% despite beating estimates for second-quarter adjusted profit, while Imperial Oil fell 2% despite reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings. In contrast, financials advanced, with RBC, TD Bank, and BMO adding about 0.5% each. Meanwhile, a first estimate showed the Canadian economy grew 0.8% in the second quarter, the most in nearly two years, to show some resiliency to inflatonary pressure.

title: Baltic Dry Index Rises on Friday, Logs Monthly Gain
summary: The Baltic dry index rose 2.2% to 2,732 on Friday, its highest level since July 27. The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, advanced 3.1% to 4,296, its highest level in two weeks. The panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, increased 2.3% to an over one-week high of 2,087. On the other hand, the supramax index decreased to 1,609, its lowest level since June 8. Considering July, the Baltic dry index rose 9.2%.

title: German Bund Yields Surge as ECB Rate Hike Bets Intensify
summary: Germany's 10-year Bund yield climbed toward 3.2%, approaching the 15-year high reached last week and posting a gain of more than 30 basis points in July, its largest monthly increase since March. The policy-sensitive two-year Bund yield also rose over 25 basis points as investors ramped up bets on further ECB rate hikes amid concerns that the Middle East conflict could fuel longer-term inflation. Money markets now fully price the ECB's deposit rate at 2.75% by early 2027, implying two additional rate hikes, with the first potentially as soon as September. Expectations were reinforced by stronger-than-expected eurozone data, with the economy expanding 0.4% in the second quarter, above forecasts of 0.2% and marking its fastest growth since early 2025. Annual inflation also accelerated to 2.9% in July, while core and services inflation strengthened. In the US, the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged this week, with markets expecting two rate hikes by June next year.

title: US Stocks Reverse Course
summary: US equities swung lower on Friday as chip producers erased their gains, while a fresh increase in long-term Treasury yields pressured broader sectors. The S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq 100 were around 0.4% down, with the latter having reached a 1.6% jump after the open. Apple tanked nearly 10% as the shortage for chips raised costs and dented production in the June quarter, denting earnings. Conversely, Amazon surged 13% after beating expectations on its cloud-computing arm. Micron, Sandisk, and Qualcomm reversed to losses of between 3% and 6%, reflecting uncertainty on volatility around AI trades. Meanwhile, broader sectors also fell with Netflix and Eli Lilly falling 3% each. The 30-year Treasury yield surged further to 19-year highs on concerns that Kevin Warsh's FOMC could refrain from raising rates to fight inflation. Also, ExxonMobil sank 3% as limited refinery capacity prevented the oil giant form higher windfalls in oil profits last quarter.

title: Pound Posts 1% Monthly Gain
summary: The pound ended July just above $1.34, gaining more than 1% against the US dollar as investors reassessed the Bank of England's latest policy decision and welcomed easing political uncertainty following the appointment of the UK's seventh prime minister in a decade. The new government also pledged to maintain fiscal discipline, supporting investor confidence. The BoE voted 6-3 to leave interest rates unchanged, with three policymakers backing a rate hike versus expectations for a 7-2 split. However, Governor Andrew Bailey downplayed expectations of an imminent tightening cycle, saying the disinflation process remains on track, while some officials suggested rate cuts could return to the agenda if the Iran conflict subsides. Markets now price in just one BoE rate hike by year-end. In the US, the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged this week, with investors expecting two rate hikes by June next year as renewed US-Iran hostilities continue to cloud the economic outlook.

title: Oil Set for Strong Monthly Advance
summary: Crude oil climbed above $85 a barrel on Friday, extending its monthly advance to more than 20% amid renewed hostilities between the US and Iran and reports that some tankers were forced to turn around in the Strait of Hormuz. According to Iran’s Fars news agency, the Revolutionary Guards stopped two tankers from passing through the waterway, while four others altered course. Even so, Kpler ship-tracking data showed that two very large crude carriers loaded in the Gulf successfully exited the Strait on Friday. The conflict has intensified this month as a temporary pause in fighting between Washington and Tehran collapsed, Yemen’s Houthis became more involved, and Saudi forces joined US operations against Iran-backed groups in Iraq. Separately, declining US crude inventories and a Ukrainian strike on Russia’s Volgograd oil refinery added to concerns over global supply.

title: Dollar Suffers Biggest Weekly Loss in Three Months
summary: The dollar index rebounded to 100.3 on Friday but remained down nearly 1.5% for the week, marking its worst weekly performance in three months and bringing its monthly decline to 1.3%. The greenback came under pressure as investors questioned whether the Federal Reserve is doing enough to bring inflation back to target. The Fed left the federal funds rate unchanged for a fifth consecutive meeting this week. While Chair Warsh reiterated the central bank's commitment to restoring price stability, he offered little guidance on the policy outlook for the remainder of the year. As a result, expectations for a rate hike at the September meeting eased, although markets continue to price in roughly a two-thirds probability of a 25bps increase.

title: Chicago Business Barometer Rises in July
summary: The Chicago Business Barometer rose to 57.6 in July 2026 from 56.7 in the previous month, remaining in expansionary territory for a third straight month and topping market expectations of 56.0. The increase was driven by new orders, which climbed to their highest level since January 2022. Meanwhile, supplier deliveries weakened, while order backlogs slipped back into contraction after two months above the neutral 50 mark. Employment remained in contraction for a fifth consecutive month, falling to its lowest level since March, while production eased but stayed in expansion. Prices paid was little changed, as respondents continued to cite geopolitical tensions and elevated energy costs despite signs of improving price stability.

title: Gold Logs First Monthly Gain Since February
summary: Gold fell to around $4,040 an ounce on Friday as the dollar rebounded from a more than one-month low. Still, the metal gained about 0.5% in July, its first monthly increase since February, supported by softer US inflation data and the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged. Gains were capped by expectations of tighter monetary policy, with markets pricing in about a 65% chance of a Fed rate hike in September. While Chair Kevin Warsh reaffirmed the Fed's commitment to lowering inflation without signaling an imminent hike, the three officials who dissented this week reiterated on Friday that further tightening is needed. Meanwhile, renewed US-Iran hostilities continued to cloud the outlook, with fresh US strikes on Iranian targets reducing hopes for a near-term diplomatic resolution. Since the conflict erupted in late February, higher oil prices have fueled inflation concerns and weighed on gold by strengthening expectations for higher interest rates.

title: FX Updates: South Korean Won Drops by 1.07%
summary: Top currency losers are South Korean Won (-1.07%), Swiss Franc (-0.51%), Euro (-0.20%) and British Pound (-0.06%). Gains are led by Norwegian Krone (0.49%), Dollar Index (0.25%) and Japanese Yen (0.19%).

title: Colombia Unemployment Rate Holds at 8%
summary: Colombia's unemployment rate held steady at 8% in June 2026, unchanged from the previous month and slightly below market expectations of 8.1%. The unemployment rate stood at 9.9% for women and 6.6% for men, resulting in a gender gap of 3.3 percentage points. Across the country's 13 major metropolitan areas, the unemployment rate was 8.3%. The highest jobless rates were recorded in Quibdó (23.3%), Cartagena (13.2%), and Ibagué (12.8%), while Medellín Metropolitan Area (7.1%), Pereira Metropolitan Area (7.2%), and Villavicencio (7.9%) posted the lowest rates. The national employment rate stood at 59.4%. In the April-June 2026 period, the average unemployment rate was 8.3%.

title: Sri Lanka Trade Deficit Widens in June
summary: Sri Lanka's trade deficit widened to $829 million in June 2026 from $540 million a year earlier, as import growth outpaced export gains. The external sector continued to reflect the impact of developments in the Middle East. Imports rose 17.3% year-on-year to $1.97 billion, driven by a 40.2% increase in fuel import expenditure, mainly due to higher spending on refined petroleum products. Meanwhile, exports edged up 0.2% to $1.14 billion. The services account surplus narrowed 33.8% from a year earlier to $162 million, as services outflows increased faster than inflows. In the first half of 2026, the cumulative trade deficit widened to $5.5 billion from $3.3 billion in the corresponding period of 2025.

title: Canada Budget Deficit Shrinks in May
summary: Canada's federal budget deficit narrowed to CAD 0.31 billion in May 2026 from CAD 2.2 billion in the same month a year earlier. Revenues increased 12.6% year-on-year to CAD 41.94 billion, driven primarily by higher income and excise tax receipts. Meanwhile, program expenses, excluding net actuarial losses, rose 6.2% to CAD 36.68 billion, reflecting higher direct program spending and larger transfers to persons, partly offset by lower transfers to provinces, territories and municipalities. Public debt charges increased 12.7% to CAD 5.16 billion due to higher effective interest rates on a larger stock of marketable bonds. Net actuarial losses rose 23.9% to CAD 415 million, remaining unchanged from the previous month. The budgetary deficit before net actuarial losses was CAD 0.1 billion, compared to a deficit of CAD 1.86 billion in the same period a year earlier.

title: FTSE 100 Falls on Friday, Still Logs Monthly Gain
summary: The FTSE 100 edged lower on Friday due to weakness in heavyweight consumer goods, healthcare, and banking stocks. Unilever dropped more than 2%, while AstraZeneca and GSK each declined around 0.5%. Major lenders HSBC Holdings and Lloyds Banking also fell. IAG fell more than 1% after reporting second-quarter revenue below expectations, reflecting the impact of ongoing disruption from the Middle East conflict on air travel. In contrast, NatWest surged more than 4% after raising its full-year guidance and indicating it could launch additional share buybacks. Sainsbury's gained around 2% after announcing the sale of its Argos business. Energy stocks also advanced, with BP and Shell rising between 1.3% and 1.8% as oil prices extended their sharp monthly rally of more than 20%. Despite Friday's decline, the FTSE 100 finished the week up more than 1% and posted a monthly gain of roughly 3.5%, its strongest performance since February.

title: Ibovespa Edges Higher as Market Reopens After Delay
summary: The Ibovespa edged higher to trade above 177,500 on Friday after the market opening was delayed due to operational issues. The delay is expected to concentrate orders that would have been executed throughout the morning, increasing the potential for volatility. Petrobras gained nearly 0.5% amid higher oil prices. Major banks also advanced, with Itaú rising more than 1%. Vale (-0.5%) reported 2Q26 earnings and revenue above expectations and raised its 2026 guidance, but posted a 35% decline in profit. Multiplan (+0.5%) is also set to hold a conference call after reporting second-quarter net profit above market forecasts. Meanwhile, Braskem (-2%) recorded lower sales in 2Q26, pressured by weaker demand for key chemicals. On the macro front, Brazil’s gross public debt-to-GDP ratio rose to 81.9% in June from 81.0% in May. The deterioration in fiscal accounts reinforced expectations that borrowing costs may remain elevated.

title: Germany 10Y Bond Yield Hits 15-year High
summary: Germany 10 Year Government Bond Yield increased to 3.21%, the highest since May 2011. Over the past 4 weeks, Germany 10Y Bond Yield gained 33.35 basis points, and in the last 12 months, it increased 53.34 basis points.

title: US Stocks Rebound on Choppy Trading
summary: US equities rebounded on a choppy Friday amid more volatility for the AI infrastructure sector as markets considered the impact of higher long-term rates. The S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq 100 were around 0.4% up. Amazon surged 15% after beating expectations on its cloud-computing arm. Software and hyperscalers were also higher on reconsidered sentiment in the AI trade, with Alphabet gaining 6% while Microsoft and Meta rose nearly 3%. On the other hand, Apple tanked 10% as the shortage for chips raised costs and lowered production in the June quarter, denting earnings. Meanwhile, broader sectors also softened with Netflix and Eli Lilly losing 3% each. The 30-year Treasury yield surged further to 19-year highs on concerns that Kevin Warsh's FOMC could refrain from raising rates to fight inflation. Also, ExxonMobil sank 3% as limited refinery capacity prevented the oil giant form higher windfalls in oil profits last quarter.

title: Week Ahead - Aug 3rd
summary: The start of August will see the war between Iran and the US continue to uphold the uncertainty in global energy prices, and consequently, the inflation outlook. This is in tandem with volatility in the AI trade, to be updated with results from SpaceX and AMD. A busy week of economic data will be headlined by the US jobs report and other labor data in the JOLTS and ADP report. ISM PMIs, factory orders, and the trade balance will also be featured for updates on industry and tariffs. In Europe, industrial production among the largest Eurozone states will unveil the impact of higher power costs, while Germany will post its trade balance. PMI results and the trade balance are awaited in China. Meanwhile, Japan will release wage data, and industry surveys are due in Australia. Interest rate decisions will take place in Brazil and India. Elsewhere, OPEC+ members will convene and discuss oil output quotas for the year.

title: Crypto Updates: Bitcoin Depreciates by 2.66%
summary: Top crypto losers are Bitcoin (-2.66%) and Ether (-2.58%).

title: Uruguay Trade Balance Swings to Deficit in June
summary: Uruguay’s trade balance swung to a deficit of $71.7 million in June 2026 from a surplus of $274.8 million a year earlier. Imports surged 35.5% year-on-year to $1.18 billion, driven by a 57% increase in intermediate goods. Purchases of electricity soared 1,286.1%, while imports of oil and distillates jumped 407.7%. Meanwhile, consumer goods imports rose 13.2% and capital goods imports increased 12.7%. Exports fell 3.2% to $1.11 billion, as shipments of electricity, gas, and water plunged 87%. Exports of primary products also declined 14.8%, while manufactured goods exports increased 7.3%.

title: Colombia Holds Interest Rate at 12.0%
summary: Colombia's central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 12.0% on July 31st. The bank noted that annual inflation rose to 6.1% in June, driven by higher food and regulated prices, while core inflation held steady at 6.0%. Inflation expectations for end-2026 and 2027 increased to 6.6% and 5.0%, respectively, with market-based expectations remaining above 6.0%. The bank also noted that economic activity strengthened in the second quarter, supported by robust services sector growth, and maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 2.5%. The unemployment rate fell to 8.0% in June. A stronger Colombian peso has helped ease inflationary pressures, but risks from the Middle East conflict and a potential El Niño event could fuel inflation and weigh on growth. Future policy decisions will remain data dependent.

title: US Stocks Close Higher on Tech Gains
summary: US stock indices closed higher on Friday as gains in major technology stocks lifted the market late in a volatile session. The S&P 500 rose 0.7%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.6%, and the Dow added 277 points. Amazon jumped 15.3% on strong cloud growth. Optimism around the AI trade boosted software and hyperscalers, with Alphabet gaining 6.9%, Microsoft adding 3%, and Meta rising 3.3%. Those gains outweighed a decline in Apple (-7.3%), after chip shortages raised costs and reduced June-quarter production, weighing on earnings. Elsewhere, broader sectors were weaker, with Netflix down 2% and Eli Lilly losing 0.6%. ExxonMobil fell 1% as limited refinery capacity prevented the oil major from fully benefiting from higher oil prices last quarter. Meanwhile, the 30-year Treasury yield climbed further on concerns that Kevin Warsh's FOMC may refrain from raising rates to curb inflation.

title: TSX Falls as Mining and Tech Losses Weigh
summary: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 0.8% to close at 35,226 on Friday, pressured by losses in mining and technology stocks. Gold miners declined as gold prices weakened amid a sharp rise in long-term US Treasury yields, with Agnico Eagle down 3.6%, Barrick losing 2.5%, and WPM falling 3.9%. Technology shares also underperformed, led by Shopify (-4.3%) and Celestica (-6%), as investors turned cautious ahead of Shopify's 2Q26 earnings on August 5. Fairfax Financial (-0.5%) and Cameco (-2.1%) reported revenue above expectations but missed EPS estimates. Enbridge slipped 1.8% despite beating forecasts for adjusted second-quarter profit. Telus plunged 11.3% after posting a second-quarter loss and resetting its quarterly dividend. Meanwhile, Imperial Oil rose 0.5% on stronger-than-expected earnings, while ATD gained 1.4% after announcing plans to acquire Poland's Zabka.

title: Ibovespa Rises Despite Trading Delay
summary: The Ibovespa rose 0.5% to close at 177,999 on Friday as investors digested Vale's earnings and Santander's tender offer to repurchase shares in Brazil. Santander surged 15.2% following the announcement. Vale added 0.2% after reporting 2Q26 earnings and revenue above expectations and raising its 2026 guidance, despite a 35% drop in profit. Petrobras extended gains, rising 1.3% as oil prices climbed amid renewed tensions between the US and Iran. WEG (+0.8%), Sabesp (+1.1%), Rede D'Or (+0.6%), and Embraer (+0.9%) also advanced. Trading opened later than scheduled due to an operational failure at the stock exchange, raising concerns about market reliability, particularly among foreign investors. On the macro front, Brazil's gross public debt-to-GDP ratio rose to 81.9% in June from 81.0% in May, reinforcing expectations that borrowing costs may remain elevated.

title: Crude Posts Best Monthly Gain Since March
summary: Crude oil prices rose 1% on Friday to finish just below $85 a barrel, capping a more than 20% gain in July, its strongest monthly increase since March, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions and growing concerns over global oil supplies. Iran claimed it attacked two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz under US military escort, though Western maritime authorities have not confirmed the incident. Renewed conflict between the US and Iran, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, and Saudi strikes on Iran-backed groups have heightened risks to key shipping routes. Falling US crude inventories have added further upward pressure on prices. Meanwhile, attacks near Russia’s Black Sea oil export infrastructure, including the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) terminal, have raised concerns about disruptions to Kazakhstan’s oil exports, an important source for European refiners. Although the CPC decided to continue operations, uncertainty over supply security continues to support higher oil prices.

title: South Korea Import Growth Remains Solid
summary: South Korea’s imports rose 26.5% year-on-year in July 2026, slowing from a 30.0% surge in the prior month and roughly in line with market forecasts of 26.6%, flash data showed. It marked the ninth consecutive month of import growth, supported by resilient domestic demand as concerns over trade disruptions stemming from the Middle East conflict eased.

title: South Korea Trade Surplus Beats Estimates
summary: South Korea’s trade surplus surged to USD 30.32 billion in July 2026, up from USD 6.61 billion in the same month a year earlier, surpassing market estimates of USD 29.59 billion and marking the 18th consecutive month of surplus, flash data showed, as exports grew much more than imports. Exports soared 62.8% year-on-year to USD 98.89 billion, easing from a downwardly revised 70.7% surge in June, mainly driven by a jump in semiconductor exports. Meanwhile, imports climbed 26.5% year-on-year to a record high of USD 68.56 billion, slowing from a downwardly revised 30.0% growth in June, supported by resilient domestic demand.

title: South Korea Export Growth Above Forecasts
summary: Exports soared 62.8% year-on-year to USD 98.89 billion in July 2026, surpassing market estimates of 59.0%, though easing from a downwardly revised 70.7% surge in June. Shipments rose for the 14th consecutive month, driven by strong demand for memory chips.

title: Czech Republic Credit Ratings Affirm at AA- with Stable Outlook
summary: Fitch Ratings affirmed the Czech Republic’s long-term foreign- and local-currency issuer default ratings at ‘AA-’ with a Stable Outlook, highlighting credible macroeconomic policies, strong institutions, and a solid external balance sheet. Fiscal deficits are set to widen under the new coalition’s looser stance, but Fitch expects easing to remain contained, keeping debt below peer medians. Growth prospects are robust, supporting income convergence with richer EU members, though risks arise from the government’s confrontational tone toward the EU on migration and climate policy. EU fund disbursements are not seen as jeopardized, and overall resilience persists despite fiscal pressures. Standard & Poor's credit rating for Czech Republic stands at AA- with stable outlook. Moody's credit rating for Czech Republic was last set at Aa3 with stable outlook, and DBRS' credit rating was last reported at AA with stable outlook.

title: Crypto Updates: Binance Depreciates by 1.45%
summary: Today's cryptos market is characterized by modest daily movements, with Binance standing out as the frontrunner with a -1.45% decrease.

title: New Zealand Building Permits Fall 3.6% in June
summary: Building consents for new dwellings in New Zealand dropped 3.6% month-on-month in June 2026, following an upwardly revised 4.9% decline in May, marking the third decline so far this year. A total of 3,741 new dwellings were consented, including 1,658 stand-alone houses, 1,614 townhouses, 132 retirement village units, and 67 apartments. In the year ended June 2026, the total number of new dwellings consented was 40,581, up 19% from the year ended June 2025. Meanwhile, New Zealand recorded 7.6 new dwelling consents per 1,000 residents, up from 6.4 per 1,000 in the previous year. The record number of new dwelling consents per 1,000 residents was 13.4 in the year ended December 1973.

title: New Zealand Stocks Edge Higher to Start the Month
summary: New Zealand's stocks rose 27 points, or 0.2%, to 13,726 in Monday morning trade, erasing losses from the previous session, mainly buoyed by the technology, communication services, and real estate sectors. The broader index tracked gains in US stock futures following an upbeat session on Wall Street on Friday, supported by a rally in technology stocks. However, traders remained cautious ahead of the release of New Zealand's unemployment data due later this week. Caution also prevailed ahead of the release of China's private-sector PMI, after last week's official survey showed the manufacturing sector in New Zealand's top trading partner had returned to contraction. A slew of US data will also be released this week, including jobs data. On the data front, New Zealand building permits dropped 3.6% in June after an upwardly revised 4.9% increase in May. Among the best performers were Chorus (1.4%), Colonial Motor (1.3%), Freightways Group (0.7%), Ebos Group (0.5%), and ANZ Group (0.4%).

title: Australia Home Prices Post Biggest Drop Since 2022
summary: Australia’s Cotality Home Value Index dropped 0.7% month over month in July 2026, marking the sharpest monthly decline since December 2022 and accelerating from a 0.4% fall in the previous month. The downturn was driven by higher borrowing costs, affordability pressures, and weaker consumer sentiment that continued to weigh on housing demand. Among the major capitals, Sydney and Melbourne continued to lead the losses, with home values falling 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively. The weakness also spread to previously resilient markets, with Brisbane declining 0.6% and Adelaide slipping 0.2%, marking their second straight monthly decline, while Perth posted a modest 0.1% gain after contracting in June. Regional markets also softened, with the combined regional index falling 0.2%, its first monthly decline since January 2023. Despite the monthly setback, Australian home prices remained 5.3% higher than a year ago in July.

title: Australia Manufacturing PMI Revised Upward
summary: The S&P Global Australia Manufacturing PMI was revised higher to 52.0 in July 2026 from the preliminary estimate of 51.7 and after a final reading of 51.5 in the previous month. Still, it marked the strongest expansion since January, as output and new orders returned to growth. The latest reading also signaled a fourth consecutive month of expansion, with output and new orders rising for the first time in five months, although the pace of growth remained only marginal. However, export orders continued to decline, reflecting persistent weakness in external demand.
